title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄序
今天子御極之七年爲嘉靖戊子天
下當鄉試之期前此諸藩類聘
學職以司考校往往受成而已
頃大臣上言以爲非法意
天子是之始
詔選京朝官以涖厥事維時江西
===
巡撫都御史周〔廣〕提督軍務都
御史汪〔鋐〕巡按御史儲〔良材〕素
加意學校謂茲賔興創舉乃趣
守臣以考試官請而署郎中〔臣〕
〔襄〕主事〔臣應埈〕受
命以往比至則士之援于提學副使
〔趙淵〕者三千有奇三試之得九
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄序

今天子御極之七年，爲嘉靖戊子，天下當鄉試之期。前此，諸藩類聘學職以司考校，往往受成而已。頃，大臣上言，以爲非法意。天子是之，始詔選京朝官以涖厥事。維時，江西巡撫都御史周〔廣〕、提督軍務都御史汪〔鋐〕、巡按御史儲〔良材〕素加意學校，謂茲賔興創舉，乃趣守臣以考試官請，而署郎中〔臣〕〔襄〕、主事〔臣應埈〕受命以往。比至，則士之援于提學副使〔趙淵〕者三千有奇，三試之，得九
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

The seventh year of the present Emperor’s reign was the wuzi year of Jiajing [1528], when Provincial Examinations were due throughout the realm. Previously, the provincial authorities had generally engaged educational officials to oversee the assessment of candidates, often merely accepting the results already determined. Recently, a high minister submitted a memorial arguing that this did not accord with the intent of the regulations. The Emperor agreed and for the first time decreed that officials serving in the capital be selected to preside over this work.

At that time, Zhou Guang, Grand Coordinator of Jiangxi and Censor-in-chief; Wang Hong, Censor-in-chief supervising military affairs; and Chu Liangcai, Regional Inspector, had long devoted particular attention to the schools. Regarding this new arrangement for recommending worthy men as an important innovation, they urged the responsible local officials to request Examiners. Your servants Xiang, Acting Bureau Director, and Ying Jun, Secretary, received orders to go. By the time we arrived, more than three thousand scholars had been put forward [?] by Zhao Yuan, Vice Commissioner for the supervision of education. After examining them in three sessions, we selected ninety-…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
十有五人焉次第其名氏若文
之優者爲錄以獻臣襄當序諸
首臣惟江西今之大邦也當吳
楚閩粤之交若匡廬彭蠡皆極
天下壯觀元精靈氣之所鍾昔
人謂橘柚之包竹箭之美不能
當也而於人才乎發之其稱雄
也久矣我
===
太祖高皇帝始定大業即
詔行科舉而進士第一人首出是
邦自是文治日洽科目彌盛名
在鼎甲者歲有其人晋而懋德
策勲表著風節爲時名臣者不
可勝紀蓋
punctuated:
十有五人焉。次第其名氏，若文之優者，爲錄以獻。臣襄當序諸首。臣惟江西，今之大邦也，當吳、楚、閩、粤之交，若匡廬、彭蠡，皆極天下壯觀，元精靈氣之所鍾。昔人謂橘柚之包、竹箭之美不能當也，而於人才乎發之，其稱雄也久矣。
我太祖高皇帝始定大業，即詔行科舉，而進士第一人首出是邦。自是文治日洽，科目彌盛，名在鼎甲者歲有其人。晋而懋德策勲，表著風節，爲時名臣者，不可勝紀。蓋
translation_en:
…ninety-five men were selected. Their names were arranged in order, together with the finest essays, and compiled into a record for presentation to the throne. Your servant Xiang was charged with writing a preface at its beginning. Your servant considers Jiangxi a great province of the present day. It lies at the meeting of Wu, Chu, Min, and Yue. Such places as Kuanglu and Pengli rank among the grandest sights under Heaven, where primordial essence and numinous vital energy concentrate. People of old said that even its tribute bundles of oranges and pomelos and its fine arrow bamboo could not match this grandeur. When this potency manifests itself in human talent, Jiangxi has long enjoyed preeminence.
As soon as our Emperor Taizu Gao established his great imperial enterprise, he decreed that the civil-service examinations be held, and the first metropolitan graduate (jinshi) to rank first came from this province. Thereafter, civil governance flourished day by day, and success in the examinations grew ever more abundant; year after year, men from here ranked among the top three. Those who advanced in office, cultivated virtue, earned recorded distinctions, displayed integrity and steadfast principle, and became renowned ministers of their times are too numerous to recount. Indeed, …

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖澤之所涵育而化成者其效固若
此不獨山川之為助也肆我
皇上大興文教屢
詔所司慎簡師儒申嚴條約海內
之士翕然嚮風雖偏州小邑皆
有人焉思自奮起而况多士如
是邦者乎其文之炳然蔚然固
宜有倍蓰於前者而臣等乃獲
===
縱觀以考校之非其幸與雖然
亦竊有懼也夫設科以取士所
來乎士者徵獨以文而已非文
則無以取之其取之也亦謂其
言之不畔乎道云耳世固有語
言若幾於道而中無所有者一
punctuated:
聖澤之所涵育而化成者，其效固若此，不獨山川之為助也。肆我皇上大興文教，屢詔所司慎簡師儒，申嚴條約。海內之士翕然嚮風，雖偏州小邑，皆有人焉思自奮起，而况多士如是邦者乎？其文之炳然蔚然，固宜有倍蓰於前者，而臣等乃獲縱觀以考校之，非其幸與？
雖然，亦竊有懼也。夫設科以取士，所來乎士者，徵獨以文而已，非文則無以取之。其取之也，亦謂其言之不畔乎道云耳。世固有語言若幾於道而中無所有者，一
translation_en:
…Such, indeed, are the results of nurture and transformation through the sage sovereign’s beneficence; they are not due solely to the assistance of the mountains and rivers. Now our Emperor has greatly promoted literary learning and moral instruction, repeatedly commanding the responsible authorities to select learned teachers with care and to reiterate and rigorously enforce the regulations. Scholars throughout the realm have responded as one to his influence. Even in remote prefectures and small counties, there are men intent on rousing themselves to exertion. How much more must this be true of a province such as this, with its many scholars! The brilliance and richness of their writing should surely surpass that of earlier times severalfold. That we, his servants, have been able to survey it fully and assess it—is this not our good fortune?
Yet we also privately feel apprehension. Examinations are established to select scholars, and the evidence sought from them [?] consists solely of their writing; without writing, there would be no means of selecting them. In selecting them, we merely judge that their words do not depart from the Way. Yet there certainly are men whose language seems close to the Way but who possess nothing within. Once…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
忝高第視所學如弁髦焉淪棄之
名檢無所不至使人指而議之
以為科目之疵蓋學不聞道而
徒以文獲薦者非有司之所深
懼與雖然所謂道者亦非有出
於文之外也士自始學誦其書
習其語言以至於今而藉以致
===
用者皆是也豈終身由之而有
不知乎匡廬彭蠡之為大夫人
能言之能歷談而無謬者必嘗
登涉焉以窮其勝者也諸士之
於道也若是焉斯不畔矣〔襄〕不
斂願相與勗其成無亦使人疵
而議之庶乎
punctuated: 忝高第，視所學如弁髦焉，淪棄之，名檢無所不至，使人指而議之，以為科目之疵。蓋學不聞道，而徒以文獲薦者，非有司之所深懼與？雖然，所謂道者，亦非有出於文之外也。士自始學，誦其書，習其語言，以至於今，而藉以致用者，皆是也。豈終身由之而有不知乎？匡廬、彭蠡之為大，夫人能言之；能歷談而無謬者，必嘗登涉焉，以窮其勝者也。諸士之於道也若是焉，斯不畔矣。〔襄〕不斂，願相與勗其成，無亦使人疵而議之，庶乎
translation_en:
…once they undeservedly attain a high examination ranking, they regard what they have learned as a discarded cap or forelock and cast it aside. Their abandonment of reputation and proper conduct knows no bounds [?], prompting others to point at them and criticize them as a blemish on the examination system. Surely those whose studies have not brought them an understanding of the Way, but who gain recommendation solely through their writing, are a source of profound concern to the responsible officials?

Nevertheless, what we call the Way does not lie outside writing. From the beginning of their studies, scholars have recited these books and practiced their language down to the present; these are also what they draw upon to put their learning into practice. Could they follow the Way throughout their lives yet remain ignorant of it? Anyone can speak of the grandeur of Kuanglu and Pengli. But those who can describe them in detail without error must have climbed the mountain and traversed the lake themselves, fully exploring their splendid scenery. If you scholars approach the Way in this manner, you will not depart from it.

I, 〔Xiang〕, presumptuously [?] wish to join you in encouraging the fulfillment of your learning. Do not give others cause to find fault and criticize you; then perhaps …

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
皇上更化之意也是舉也同考試則
學正吳〔彥良〕教諭沈〔暄公溥〕何
曾〔志澄〕張〔元秋〕白〔緣〕羅〔士賔〕訓
導胡〔愘〕祝〔廷玉〕任〔柱〕提調則布
政使顧〔珀〕黃〔芳〕監試則按察使
胡〔璉〕副使林〔大輅〕御史〔良材〕實
監臨之百凡飭備勞實倍焉先
===
後恊賛有勞於法得書則有叅
政方〔楷〕李〔緋〕叅議陳〔沂〕邵〔天和〕
鍾〔雲瑞〕副使陳〔桓〕羅〔輅〕僉事陳
〔璧〕王〔暐〕吳〔瀚〕令〔楷〕〔瀚〕以公出〔天〕
〔和〕以遷云其餘列之各執事之
下可考也
兵部職方清吏司署郎中事立
punctuated:
皇上更化之意也。是舉也，同考試則學正吳〔彥良〕、教諭沈〔暄公溥〕、何曾〔志澄〕、張〔元秋〕、白〔緣〕、羅〔士賔〕，訓導胡〔愘〕、祝〔廷玉〕、任〔柱〕；提調則布政使顧〔珀〕、黃〔芳〕；監試則按察使胡〔璉〕、副使林〔大輅〕。御史〔良材〕實監臨之，百凡飭備，勞實倍焉。先後恊賛，有勞於法得書，則有叅政方〔楷〕、李〔緋〕，叅議陳〔沂〕、邵〔天和〕、鍾〔雲瑞〕，副使陳〔桓〕、羅〔輅〕，僉事陳〔璧〕、王〔暐〕、吳〔瀚〕。令〔楷〕〔瀚〕以公出，〔天〕〔和〕以遷云。其餘列之各執事之下，可考也。
兵部職方清吏司署郎中事立
translation_en:
…His Majesty’s intention to bring about reform.
For this examination, the Associate Examiners were Wu Yanliang, an Instructor in a subprefectural school; Shen Xuan Gongpu [?], He Zeng Zhicheng [?], Zhang Yuanqiu, Bai Yuan, and Luo Shibin, Instructors in county schools; and Hu Ke [?], Zhu Tingyu, and Ren Zhu, Assistant Instructors. The Proctors were Provincial Administration Commissioners Gu Po and Huang Fang. Those monitoring the examination were Surveillance Commissioner Hu Lian and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Lin Dalu. Censor Liangcai served as the Supervising Official. He put every arrangement in order and ensured that everything was ready, his labors truly twice those of others.
Those who assisted throughout, whose services entitled them under the regulations to be recorded, were Provincial Administration Vice Commissioners Fang Kai and Li Fei; Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioners Chen Yi, Shao Tianhe, and Zhong Yunrui; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Chen Huan and Luo Lu; and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Chen Bi, Wang Wei, and Wu Han. At present [?], Kai and Han were away on official business, and Tianhe had been transferred. The others are listed under their respective duties and may be consulted there.
Acting Director of the Bureau of Military Operations in the Ministry of War, [立 unclear] …

translation_en: … Lu Xiang respectfully composed this preface.

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖七年江西鄉試
監臨官
巡按江西監察御史儲良材〔邦掄廣西馬平縣籍湖 廣襄陽縣人丁丑進士〕
提調官
江西等處承宣布政使司左布政使顧　珀〔載祥福建晉江縣人 己未進士〕
江西等處承宣布政使司右布政使黃　芳〔仲實廣東崖州所人 戊辰進士〕

河南彰德府磁州儒學學正吳彥良〔遂之廣東瓊山縣人 癸酉貢士〕
福建福寧州福安縣儒學教諭沈　暄〔景和直隸華亭縣人 丙子貢士〕
福建福州府福清縣儒學教諭何公溥〔一卿廣東博羅縣人 己卯貢士〕
河南開封府儀封縣儒學教諭曾志澄〔揚卿福建莆田縣人 壬午貢士〕

punctuated:
嘉靖七年江西鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按江西監察御史儲良材〔邦掄，廣西馬平縣籍，湖 廣襄陽縣人，丁丑進士〕。

江西等處承宣布政使司左布政使顧　珀〔載祥，福建晉江縣人，己未進士〕。
江西等處承宣布政使司右布政使黃　芳〔仲實，廣東崖州所人，戊辰進士〕。

監試官：
江西等處提刑按察司按察使胡　璉〔重器，直隸沭陽縣人，乙丑進士〕。
江西等處提刑按察司副使林大輅〔以乘，福建莆田縣人，甲戌進士〕。

兵部職方清吏司署郎中事主事盧　襄〔師陳，直隸吳縣人，癸未進士〕。

同考試官：
河南彰德府磁州儒學學正吳彥良〔遂之，廣東瓊山縣人，癸酉貢士〕。
福建福寧州福安縣儒學教諭沈　暄〔景和，直隸華亭縣人，丙子貢士〕。
福建福州府福清縣儒學教諭何公溥〔一卿，廣東博羅縣人，己卯貢士〕。
河南開封府儀封縣儒學教諭曾志澄〔揚卿，福建莆田縣人，壬午貢士〕。

translation_en:
Jiangxi Provincial Examination, seventh year of Jiajing (1528).

Supervising Official
Chu Liangcai, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Banglun. He was registered in Maping County, Guangxi, and was a native of Xiangyang County, Huguang; he became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the dingchou year.

Proctors
Gu Po, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Zaixiang. He was a native of Jinjiang County, Fujian, and became a metropolitan graduate in the jiwei year.
Huang Fang, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Zhongshi. He was a native of the Yazhou military station, Guangdong, and became a metropolitan graduate in the wuchen year.

Examination Monitors
Hu Lian, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Zhongqi. He was a native of Shuyang County, Zhili, and became a metropolitan graduate in the yichou year.
Lin Dalu, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Yicheng. He was a native of Putian County, Fujian, and became a metropolitan graduate in the jiaxu year.

Examiners
Lu Xiang, Secretary acting as Director of the Bureau of Military Operations in the Ministry of War, had the courtesy name Shichen. He was a native of Wu County, Zhili, and became a metropolitan graduate in the guiwei year.
Tu Yingjun, Secretary in the Guizhou Bureau of the Ministry of Justice, had the courtesy name Wensheng. He was a native of Pinghu County, Zhejiang, and became a metropolitan graduate in the bingxu year.

Associate Examiners
Wu Yanliang, Director of the Confucian School of Ci Subprefecture, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Suizhi. He was a native of Qiongshan County, Guangdong, and became a tribute student (gongshi) in the guiyou year.
Shen Xuan, Instructor at the Confucian School of Fu'an County, Funing Subprefecture, Fujian, had the courtesy name Jinghe. He was a native of Huating County, Zhili, and became a tribute student in the bingzi year.
He Gongpu, Instructor at the Confucian School of Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, had the courtesy name Yiqing. He was a native of Boluo County, Guangdong, and became a tribute student in the jimao year.
Zeng Zhicheng, Instructor at the Confucian School of Yifeng County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Yangqing. He was a native of Putian County, Fujian, and became a tribute student in the renwu year.
Zhang Yuanzhi, Instructor at the Confucian School of Jiande County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Jingshi. He was a native of Min County, Fujian, and became a tribute student in the yiyou year.

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
臨之以莊則敬孝慈則忠舉善而教不能
則勸
舜好問而好察邇言隱惡而揚善執其兩
端用其中於民
萬物皆備於我矣反身而誠樂莫大焉強
恕而行求仁莫近焉
易
===
乾道變化各正性命保合大和乃利貞
解利西南往得衆也其來復吉乃得中也
有攸往夙吉往有功也
是故法象莫大乎天地變通莫大乎四時
縣象著明莫大乎日月崇高莫大乎富
貴備物致用立成器以爲天下利莫大
乎聖人探賾索隱鉤深致遠以定天下
之吉凶成天下之亹亹者莫大乎蓍龜
井居其所而遷巽稱而隱
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

臨之以莊，則敬；孝慈，則忠；舉善而教不能，則勸。

舜好問，而好察邇言，隱惡而揚善，執其兩端，用其中於民。

萬物皆備於我矣。反身而誠，樂莫大焉；強恕而行，求仁莫近焉。

易

乾道變化，各正性命，保合大和，乃利貞。

解，利西南，往得衆也；其來復吉，乃得中也；有攸往，夙吉，往有功也。

是故法象莫大乎天地，變通莫大乎四時，縣象著明莫大乎日月，崇高莫大乎富貴，備物致用、立成器以爲天下利莫大乎聖人，探賾索隱、鉤深致遠，以定天下之吉凶、成天下之亹亹者，莫大乎蓍龜。

井，居其所而遷；巽，稱而隱。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“If you preside over the people with dignity, they will be respectful; if you are filial and compassionate, they will be loyal; if you advance the good and teach those who lack ability, they will be encouraged.”

“Shun delighted in asking questions and examining even ordinary remarks. He concealed what was bad and made known what was good. He grasped the two extremes and applied the mean between them to the people.”

“All things are fully present within me. To turn inward and find oneself sincere—there is no greater joy. To strive to act with consideration for others—there is no nearer way to seek humaneness.”

Book of Changes

“The Way of Qian transforms and changes, allowing each thing to attain its proper nature and allotted destiny. It preserves and unites supreme harmony; thus it is beneficial and steadfast.”

“Deliverance (Jie): ‘The southwest is favorable’ means that by going there one gains the multitude. ‘Returning is auspicious’ means that one attains the center. ‘If there is somewhere to go, an early start is auspicious’ means that going brings accomplishment.”

“Thus, for models and images, nothing is greater than Heaven and Earth; for transformation and adaptation, nothing is greater than the four seasons; for images suspended above that shine brightly, nothing is greater than the sun and moon; for eminence and exaltation, nothing is greater than wealth and rank. For preparing things for use and fashioning implements to benefit all under Heaven, none is greater than the sage. For exploring mysteries and seeking what is hidden, plumbing the depths and reaching far, thereby determining good and ill fortune under Heaven and bringing the world's endeavors to fruition, nothing is greater than milfoil stalks and tortoise shells.

“The Well (Jing) remains in its place yet conveys its supply elsewhere; the Gentle (Xun) weighs things yet remains concealed.”

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
書
帝曰疇若予工僉曰垂哉帝曰俞咨垂汝
共工垂拜稽首讓于殳斨暨伯與帝曰
俞往哉汝諧帝曰疇若予上下草木鳥
獸僉曰益哉帝曰俞咨益汝作朕虞益
拜稽首讓于朱虎熊羆帝曰俞往哉汝
諧
庶土交正底慎財賦咸則三壤成賦中邦
惟辟作福惟辟作威惟辟玉食
立政任人準夫牧作三事
===
詩
維鵲有巢維鳩居之之子于歸百兩御之
維鵲有巢維鳩方之之子于歸百兩將
之維鵲有巢維鳩盈之之子于歸百兩
成之
蓼彼蕭斯零露泥泥既見君子孔燕豈弟
宜兄宜弟令德壽豈
文王在上於昭于天周雖舊邦其命維新
punctuated:
書
帝曰：「疇若予工？」僉曰：「垂哉！」帝曰：「俞！咨，垂！汝共工。」垂拜稽首，讓于殳斨暨伯與。帝曰：「俞！往哉，汝諧！」帝曰：「疇若予上下草木鳥獸？」僉曰：「益哉！」帝曰：「俞！咨，益！汝作朕虞。」益拜稽首，讓于朱、虎、熊、羆。帝曰：「俞！往哉，汝諧！」
庶土交正，底慎財賦，咸則三壤，成賦中邦。
惟辟作福，惟辟作威，惟辟玉食。
立政：任人、準夫、牧，作三事。

詩
維鵲有巢，維鳩居之。之子于歸，百兩御之。維鵲有巢，維鳩方之。之子于歸，百兩將之。維鵲有巢，維鳩盈之。之子于歸，百兩成之。
蓼彼蕭斯，零露泥泥。既見君子，孔燕豈弟。宜兄宜弟，令德壽豈。
文王在上，於昭于天！周雖舊邦，其命維新。
translation_en:
Book of Documents

The emperor said, “Who can attend to my works?” All replied, “Chui!” The emperor said, “Yes! Ah, Chui, you shall be Minister of Works.” Chui bowed and knocked his head to the ground, yielding the appointment to Shuqiang and Boyu. The emperor said, “Yes! Go and undertake it; you will bring harmony.” The emperor said, “Who can attend to the grasses, trees, birds, and beasts of my highlands and lowlands?” All replied, “Yi!” The emperor said, “Yes! Ah, Yi, you shall be my Forester.” Yi bowed and knocked his head to the ground, yielding the appointment to Zhu, Hu, Xiong, and Pi. The emperor said, “Yes! Go and undertake it; you will bring harmony.”

The various soils were compared and properly classified. The utmost care was taken over resources and levies; all assessments followed the three grades of soil, establishing the levies throughout the central realm.

Only the sovereign may confer blessings; only the sovereign may wield punitive authority; only the sovereign may enjoy precious food.

In establishing government, administrators, judicial officers, and governors constitute the three principal offices.

Book of Odes

The magpie has a nest; the dove dwells in it. This maiden goes to her marriage; a hundred carriages welcome her. The magpie has a nest; the dove occupies it. This maiden goes to her marriage; a hundred carriages escort her. The magpie has a nest; the doves fill it. This maiden goes to her marriage; a hundred carriages complete the ceremony.

Tall grows that southernwood; the falling dew lies thick upon it. Having seen the noble lord, we are greatly at ease and joyful. He is a fitting elder brother, a fitting younger brother; may his excellent virtue bring him long life and happiness.

King Wen is on high—oh, how he shines in Heaven! Though Zhou is an ancient state, its mandate is new. …

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
有周不顯帝命不時
烈文辟公錫茲祉福惠我無疆子孫保之
春秋
齊侯宋人陳人蔡人邾人會于北杏〔莊公〕
十有三年齊人陳人曹人伐宋〔莊公十〕
有四年
楚人滅黃〔僖公十有二年〕
楚子蔡侯次于厥貉〔文公十年〕公會宋公
陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯晉趙盾癸酉
同盟于新城〔文公十有四年〕
===
公圍成〔昭公二十有六年〕季孫意如會晉
荀躒于適歷〔昭公三十有一年〕
禮記
故聖人作則必以天地爲本以陰陽爲端
以四時爲柄以日星爲紀月以爲量鬼
神以爲徒五行以爲質禮義以爲器人
情以爲田四靈以爲畜
古之君子必佩玉右徵角左宮羽
punctuated:
有周不顯？帝命不時？

烈文辟公，錫茲祉福，惠我無疆，子孫保之。

春秋

齊侯、宋人、陳人、蔡人、邾人會于北杏〔莊公〕十有三年。齊人、陳人、曹人伐宋〔莊公十〕有四年。

楚人滅黃〔僖公十有二年〕。

楚子、蔡侯次于厥貉〔文公十年〕。公會宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、晉趙盾，癸酉，同盟于新城〔文公十有四年〕。

公圍成〔昭公二十有六年〕。季孫意如會晉荀躒于適歷〔昭公三十有一年〕。

禮記

故聖人作則，必以天地爲本，以陰陽爲端，以四時爲柄，以日星爲紀，月以爲量，鬼神以爲徒，五行以爲質，禮義以爲器，人情以爲田，四靈以爲畜。

古之君子必佩玉，右徵角，左宮羽。
translation_en:
…Is Zhou not illustrious? Is the Supreme Lord’s mandate not timely?

Illustrious and cultivated, you ruling lords bestow these blessings and good fortune. Your bounty to us knows no bounds; may your descendants preserve it.

Spring and Autumn Annals

The Marquis of Qi and men of Song, Chen, Cai, and Zhu met at Beixing. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhuang; the date is split irregularly in the transcription.〕 Men of Qi, Chen, and Cao attacked Song. 〔Fourteenth year of Duke Zhuang; the date is split irregularly in the transcription.〕

Men of Chu destroyed Huang. 〔Twelfth year of Duke Xi.〕

The Viscount of Chu and the Marquis of Cai encamped at Juehe. 〔Tenth year of Duke Wen.〕 The duke met with the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, and Zhao Dun of Jin. On the guiyou day, they jointly concluded a covenant at Xincheng. 〔Fourteenth year of Duke Wen.〕

The duke besieged Cheng. 〔Twenty-sixth year of Duke Zhao.〕 Jisun Yiru met with Xun Li of Jin at Shili. 〔Thirty-first year of Duke Zhao.〕

Record of Rites

Thus, when the sage establishes rules, he necessarily takes Heaven and Earth as his foundation, yin and yang as his starting point, the four seasons as his means of direction, the sun and stars as his guiding order, the moon as his measure, ghosts and spirits as his companions, the Five Phases as his substance, ritual and righteousness as his implements, human feelings as his field to cultivate, and the four numinous creatures as his domesticated animals.

The gentlemen of antiquity invariably wore jade pendants: those on the right sounded the notes zhi and jue, and those on the left, gong and yu.

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
及夫敎樂而無禮備而不偏者其唯大
聖乎
博施備物可謂不匱矣
第貳場
論
聖人一言盡天下之道
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢立王侯朝獻郡國口賦法詔〔高帝十〕
一年
===
擬唐以劉洎爲侍中岑文本馬周爲中書
令誥〔貞觀十八年〕
擬
賜翰林學士承旨宋濂醪膳諸物謝表〔洪武十年〕
判語〔五條〕
濫設官吏
賦役不均
服舍違式
優恤軍屬
punctuated:
及夫敎樂而無禮，備而不偏者，其唯大聖乎？
博施備物，可謂不匱矣。
第貳場
論
聖人一言盡天下之道。
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢立王侯朝獻、郡國口賦法詔〔高帝十〕一年。
擬唐以劉洎爲侍中、岑文本馬周爲中書令誥〔貞觀十八年〕。
擬賜翰林學士承旨宋濂醪膳諸物謝表〔洪武十年〕。
判語〔五條〕
濫設官吏。
賦役不均。
服舍違式。
優恤軍屬。
translation_en:
As for teaching music without ritual [?], yet being comprehensive and not one-sided—could this be true only of the great sage?
To bestow generously and provide all things may be called inexhaustible.

Second Session

Discourse
“The sage, in a single utterance, fully expresses the Way of all under Heaven.”

Edicts, proclamations, and memorials 〔One question from among these [?].〕
Compose an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty establishing regulations for the court offerings of kings and marquises and the poll taxes of commanderies and kingdoms. 〔Eleventh year of Emperor Gao’s reign.〕
Compose a proclamation in the manner of the Tang dynasty appointing Liu Ji as Palace Attendant and Cen Wenben and Ma Zhou as Presidents of the Secretariat. 〔Eighteenth year of Zhenguan.〕
Compose a memorial of thanks on behalf of Song Lian, Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts, for gifts of wine, prepared foods, and other items. 〔Tenth year of Hongwu.〕

Legal Judgments 〔Five items.〕
The unauthorized establishment of official and clerical posts.
Inequitable allocation of taxes and labor services.
Clothing and residences that violate prescribed standards.
Preferential relief for military dependents.

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
私鑄銅錢
第叁場
策五道
問三代以降人君以征伐得天下者必有
非常之功以慰衆望定民志若漢高帝
縞素之師光武昆陽之戰是也我
太祖高皇帝以淮甸布衣不階尺土奄有天下
渡江之初新造未集一時群雄惟陳氏
張氏爲二大敵友諒屢寇而屢破之彭
===
蠡之役卒殲渠魁以平江漢自是僣亂
悉除天命遂定神謨偉烈藏之金匱石
室固非臣下所敢窺而得於傳聞紀錄
者亦可粗陳其一二歟當時發縱謀畫
固皆斷自
聖衷不知翊戴諸臣宣力効忠伏節死義亦有
可言者歟二敵之相去友諒稍遠則攻
之宜緩而兵法乘虛則近者之襲吾後
可慮也不先近而及遠其亦有說歟古
punctuated:
私鑄銅錢。

第叁場
策五道

問：三代以降，人君以征伐得天下者，必有非常之功，以慰衆望，定民志。若漢高帝縞素之師、光武昆陽之戰是也。我太祖高皇帝以淮甸布衣，不階尺土，奄有天下。渡江之初，新造未集，一時群雄，惟陳氏、張氏爲二大敵。友諒屢寇而屢破之，彭蠡之役，卒殲渠魁，以平江漢。自是僣亂悉除，天命遂定。神謨偉烈，藏之金匱石室，固非臣下所敢窺；而得於傳聞紀錄者，亦可粗陳其一二歟？當時發縱謀畫，固皆斷自聖衷，不知翊戴諸臣宣力効忠、伏節死義，亦有可言者歟？二敵之相去，友諒稍遠，則攻之宜緩；而兵法乘虛，則近者之襲吾後，可慮也。不先近而及遠，其亦有說歟？古
translation_en:
Illicit casting of copper coinage.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: Since the Three Dynasties, rulers who gained All under Heaven through conquest have invariably performed extraordinary feats to satisfy public expectations and settle the people's hearts. Examples are Emperor Gao of Han's army clad in white mourning garments and Guangwu's battle at Kunyang. Our Emperor Taizu Gao, a commoner from the Huai region, gained possession of All under Heaven without so much as a foot of territory as his stepping-stone. When he first crossed the Yangzi, the newly founded regime was not yet firmly established. Among the contending warlords of the time, only Chen and Zhang were major enemies. Youliang repeatedly invaded and was repeatedly defeated; at the battle of Pengli, the chief rebel was finally destroyed, bringing peace to the Yangzi and Han regions. Thereafter, all usurpation and rebellion were eliminated, and the Mandate of Heaven was secured.

His divine counsels and mighty achievements are preserved in golden coffers and stone chambers: these are certainly not things that his subjects would dare to pry into. But might you briefly recount one or two of those matters known through transmitted accounts and written records? At that time, the direction of operations and the formulation of plans were, of course, all decided by his sagely judgment. Yet might there also be something to say of the ministers who supported him, exerting themselves in loyal service and laying down their lives for integrity and righteousness?

Of the two enemies, Youliang was somewhat farther away, so an attack upon him ought to have been deferred. Moreover, since military strategy calls for exploiting an opponent's vulnerability, there was reason to fear that the nearer enemy would attack our rear. Is there an explanation for attacking the more distant enemy before the nearer one? In antiquity, …

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
之以征伐得天下者其所以得之未必
盡出於征伐哉
聖祖功烈若此之盛亦豈無其說歟諸生苟有
聞也願悉著之篇毋讓曰繪天地模日
月之難爲工也
問古之稱盛治者必曰堯舜今即其書而
觀之其稱堯曰恭讓舜曰寛簡則所尚
可知也然舜有四凶之誅三苗之討豈
二帝相繼而道不相沿歟抑外爲寛簡
===
之名而内有嚴之實也自是而後禹有
禹刑之制湯有官刑之儆文王有速殺
之義然則帝王之道信乎其貴嚴歟漢
之文帝以德化民宋之仁宗忠厚立國
固皆寛仁之主矣而或謂其不如宣帝
之厲精或病其國勢之不振則君德信
以嚴爲尚而仁固其末歟聖人慎罰而
用勸王者本身而化成二者之間必有
取也今
punctuated:
之以征伐得天下者，其所以得之，未必盡出於征伐哉！聖祖功烈若此之盛，亦豈無其說歟？諸生苟有聞也，願悉著之篇，毋讓曰繪天地、模日月之難爲工也。
問：古之稱盛治者，必曰堯舜。今即其書而觀之，其稱堯曰恭讓，舜曰寛簡，則所尚可知也。然舜有四凶之誅、三苗之討，豈二帝相繼而道不相沿歟？抑外爲寛簡之名，而内有嚴之實也？自是而後，禹有禹刑之制，湯有官刑之儆，文王有速殺之義。然則帝王之道，信乎其貴嚴歟？漢之文帝以德化民，宋之仁宗忠厚立國，固皆寛仁之主矣。而或謂其不如宣帝之厲精，或病其國勢之不振，則君德信以嚴爲尚，而仁固其末歟？聖人慎罰而用勸，王者本身而化成，二者之間必有取也。今
translation_en:
…those who gained All under Heaven through conquest did not necessarily gain it entirely through conquest! With the achievements of the Sagely Founder so magnificent, surely there is an explanation for them as well? If you candidates have heard anything of this, I ask you to set it all down in your essays. Do not decline on the grounds that depicting Heaven and Earth and portraying the sun and moon are difficult to accomplish skillfully.
Policy question: Those who speak of flourishing government in antiquity invariably cite Yao and Shun. If we now examine their accounts in the Documents, Yao is described as reverent and yielding, and Shun as generous and unexacting; we can thus understand what they esteemed. Yet Shun punished the Four Malefactors and campaigned against the Sanmiao. Could it be that these two emperors succeeded one another without continuing in the same Way? Or did Shun outwardly enjoy a reputation for generosity and simplicity while inwardly practicing severity? Thereafter, Yu established the Punishments of Yu, Tang issued the admonitions of the Punishments for Officials, and King Wen upheld the principle of putting offenders swiftly to death. Does the Way of emperors and kings, then, truly prize severity? Emperor Wen of Han transformed the people through virtue, and Emperor Renzong of Song founded his rule upon sincerity and generosity. Both were certainly lenient and benevolent rulers. Yet some say that Emperor Wen fell short of Emperor Xuan in vigorous dedication, while others fault Emperor Renzong for the weakness of his state. Does a ruler’s virtue, then, truly consist above all in severity, with benevolence merely secondary? The sage exercises caution in punishment and employs encouragement; the true king takes his own conduct as the foundation and brings moral transformation to fruition. Between these two approaches, there must be something to adopt. Now…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
天子建中和之極行將見時雍之化矣而芹曝
之獻在臣子弗能已也諸生幸各陳所
見以贊
至治
問人君之馭其臣其道不一有課以考功
有謚以易名課以黜陟於一時謚以榮
辱於百世皆所以勸善而懲惡也然立
法必有所始行法必有其人而載之必
有其書可得而並聞歟就其中亦有可
===
稱者歟夫官之有課宜得人矣而黜陟
或未定以厭乎公議没而賜謚宜論定
矣而榮辱或未足以盖其平生亦可得
而略舉其人歟然考課而不釆其善最
之實狀則藻鑑必迷議謚而徒取其傳
會之虚文則斷案何在故善最雖出於
近代而君子或有取焉謚法雖稱爲古
書而識者自能辯也又可得而聞其説
歟
punctuated:
天子建中和之極，行將見時雍之化矣。而芹曝之獻，在臣子弗能已也。諸生幸各陳所見，以贊至治。

問：人君之馭其臣，其道不一。有課以考功，有謚以易名。課以黜陟於一時，謚以榮辱於百世，皆所以勸善而懲惡也。然立法必有所始，行法必有其人，而載之必有其書，可得而並聞歟？就其中亦有可稱者歟？夫官之有課，宜得人矣，而黜陟或未定以厭乎公議；没而賜謚，宜論定矣，而榮辱或未足以盖其平生，亦可得而略舉其人歟？然考課而不釆其善最之實狀，則藻鑑必迷；議謚而徒取其傳會之虚文，則斷案何在？故善最雖出於近代，而君子或有取焉；謚法雖稱爲古書，而識者自能辯也。又可得而聞其説歟？
translation_en:
…the Son of Heaven establishes the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony, and we shall soon witness a transformation bringing universal concord. Yet we, his subjects and servants, cannot refrain from offering our humble contributions, like offerings of cress and the sun’s warmth. May you students each set forth your views to assist in achieving the highest order of government.

Question: A ruler has more than one means of governing his ministers. There are evaluations to assess their achievements, and posthumous titles to replace their personal names. Evaluations bring dismissal or promotion during their lifetimes; posthumous titles bring honor or disgrace for a hundred generations. Both serve to encourage good and punish evil. Yet the establishment of these institutions must have had its beginnings; their implementation must have depended upon particular individuals; and there must be books recording them. May we hear about all of these together? Among them, are there also examples worthy of praise?

With evaluations of officials, one would expect suitable men to be secured for office; yet decisions about dismissal and promotion have sometimes failed to satisfy public opinion. When a posthumous title is conferred at death, one would expect a settled judgment; yet the honor or disgrace it conveys has sometimes proved inadequate to sum up the recipient’s life. Could you briefly name some such individuals?

If evaluations fail to draw upon factual accounts of officials’ good conduct and outstanding achievements, discerning judgment will inevitably go astray. If deliberations over posthumous titles rely merely on empty writings based on forced associations, what basis is there for a verdict? Thus, although ratings of good conduct and outstanding achievement originated in more recent times, gentlemen may find something worth adopting in them. Although the Rules for Posthumous Titles (Shifa) is called an ancient book, knowledgeable readers can discern its authenticity. May we also hear an explanation of these matters?

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
國家酌古爲治二法並行然於勸懲之效未能
盡如古昔焉其故何歟諸士子幸詳考
而備論之以爲
今日駁臣之助
問有田則有賦古之制也井田在孟子時
已不聞其詳周禮或掌之遂人或掌之
匠人無乃有不同乎漢代秦者也秦廢
井田開阡陌史稱高帝悉除秦法秦法
之不善者宜莫如廢井田也當時未聞
===
興復之舉豈輔之者非王佐而爲之有
未暇乎抑別有其說乎兩漢頗多賢君
其取民之善亦有可稱者乎井田之後
唐法最善租庸調行之未久而變爲兩
稅論者皆以兩稅爲不善而或又謂其
非法之罪其果然乎宋仍唐法其間有
不善者可得而聞乎我
朝田賦之法損益前代量地肥瘠而爲賦輕重
然多倚辦於東南近年以來逋負日積
punctuated:
國家酌古爲治，二法並行，然於勸懲之效，未能盡如古昔焉，其故何歟？諸士子幸詳考而備論之，以爲今日駁臣之助。

問：有田則有賦，古之制也。井田在孟子時，已不聞其詳。《周禮》或掌之遂人，或掌之匠人，無乃有不同乎？漢代秦者也，秦廢井田，開阡陌。史稱高帝悉除秦法，秦法之不善者，宜莫如廢井田也。當時未聞興復之舉，豈輔之者非王佐，而爲之有未暇乎？抑別有其說乎？兩漢頗多賢君，其取民之善，亦有可稱者乎？井田之後，唐法最善。租庸調行之未久，而變爲兩稅。論者皆以兩稅爲不善，而或又謂其非法之罪，其果然乎？宋仍唐法，其間有不善者，可得而聞乎？我朝田賦之法，損益前代，量地肥瘠而爲賦輕重，然多倚辦於東南。近年以來，逋負日積。
translation_en:
…Our state draws upon antiquity in its governance and employs both systems together. Yet their effectiveness in encouraging good and deterring wrongdoing has not fully matched that of ancient times. Why is this? You candidates are invited to examine the matter carefully and discuss it fully, thereby assisting the officials who offer criticism today [?; the transcription reads 駁臣].

Question: Where there is farmland, there is taxation: this was the ancient system. Even in Mengzi’s time, the details of the well-field system were no longer known. In the Rites of Zhou, responsibility for it is assigned in one place to the suiren, officials administering the rural districts, and in another to the jiangren, master craftsmen. Is there not a discrepancy here? The Han succeeded the Qin. The Qin abolished the well-field system and opened up paths running through the fields. The histories say that Emperor Gao abolished all Qin laws. Among the harmful measures of the Qin, surely none was worse than abolishing the well-field system. Yet we hear of no attempt to restore it at that time. Was this because those assisting him lacked the ability to aid a true king, and he had not yet found time to undertake it? Or is there another explanation? There were many worthy rulers during the Western and Eastern Han. Were there also commendable practices in their levying of taxes on the people?

After the well-field system, the Tang system was the best. Yet the system of grain tax, labor service or its commutation, and payment in textiles—the zu-yong-diao—had not been practiced long before it was changed into the twice-yearly tax. Commentators all regard the twice-yearly tax as unsatisfactory, but some also say that the fault did not lie with the system itself. Is this indeed so? The Song continued the Tang system. May we hear what shortcomings it contained?

Our dynasty’s land-tax system modifies those of preceding dynasties, assessing the fertility or barrenness of the land to determine whether taxes should be light or heavy. Nevertheless, it relies heavily on the southeast to supply its revenues. In recent years, unpaid tax arrears have accumulated day by day…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
倉廥日虛海內皆然東南尤甚三代之
法不可復已伊欲足國用而裕民力不
知何施而可儒者以高爲名多失之迂
俗吏以甲爲實多失之陋不迂不陋諸
士子其毋曰出位之思也佇聞其詳以
觀用世之學
問居其鄉則思其人故儒者論世而尚友
君子取善以崇德請以江右名士與諸
子議之夫人品不同或志于道學或著
===
之節義或優於文章三者果判然不相
謀歟抑可以會而兼之也故有著書立
言得其師旨有愛君憂國終始弗渝有
知誠意正心之說而不以掖垣易一記
者有懼爲顏閔所笑而不因好官見時
宰者是均之爲道學也然又有究易無
定體之旨而來天下後世儒宗之稱者
其與隱居講道深究義利之途學尊德
性復著荆門之政者果孰偉歟有使金
punctuated:
倉廥日虛，海內皆然，東南尤甚。三代之法不可復已，伊欲足國用而裕民力，不知何施而可。儒者以高爲名，多失之迂；俗吏以甲爲實，多失之陋。不迂不陋，諸士子其毋曰出位之思也。佇聞其詳，以觀用世之學。
問：居其鄉則思其人，故儒者論世而尚友，君子取善以崇德。請以江右名士與諸子議之。夫人品不同，或志于道學，或著之節義，或優於文章，三者果判然不相謀歟？抑可以會而兼之也？故有著書立言，得其師旨；有愛君憂國，終始弗渝；有知誠意正心之說，而不以掖垣易一記者；有懼爲顏閔所笑，而不因好官見時宰者。是均之爲道學也。然又有究易無定體之旨，而來天下後世儒宗之稱者，其與隱居講道，深究義利之途，學尊德性，復著荆門之政者，果孰偉歟？有使金
translation_en:
…The granaries and storehouses grow emptier by the day. This is so throughout the realm, and especially in the southeast. The institutions of the Three Dynasties can no longer be restored. Yet, wishing to provide adequately for state expenditure while easing the burden on the people's resources, we do not know what measures would work. Confucian scholars seek a reputation for loftiness and often err in being impractical; ordinary officials take jia 甲 as practical substance [?] and often err in being narrow-minded. As for a course that is neither impractical nor narrow-minded, you candidates should not say that considering it exceeds your station. We await your detailed explanations, so that we may judge your learning for service in the world.
Question: When dwelling in a region, one thinks of its people. Thus Confucian scholars consider the ages in which earlier worthies lived and seek friendship with them across time; the gentleman adopts what is good to exalt his virtue. Let us discuss with you the eminent men of Jiangyou. Human qualities differ: some devote themselves to the Learning of the Way, some distinguish themselves through integrity and righteousness, and some excel in literary composition. Are these three indeed sharply divided, with nothing in common? Or can they be brought together and united in one person? There were those who wrote books and expounded teachings, grasping their masters' purport; those who loved their sovereign and cared anxiously for their country, never wavering from beginning to end; one who understood the teaching of making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind, and would not exchange a commemorative account for a post in the Chancellery [?]; and one who feared being laughed at by Yan Hui and Min Sun, and would not visit the chief minister of his day to obtain a desirable office. All these equally exemplify the Learning of the Way. Yet there was also one who investigated the purport of the teaching that the Changes has no fixed form and thereby earned recognition throughout the realm and in later generations as a master of the Confucian tradition. Compared with the man who lived in retirement teaching the Way, deeply investigated the paths of righteousness and profit, honored the moral nature in his learning, and also distinguished himself in the government of Jingmen—which was truly the greater? There was one who went as an envoy to Jin…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
留十五年不屈而其子亦以節顯者有
被執死于越城而其孫亦以死著者有
抱印登城而死戰報國者有賁卜肆
而慟哭以卒者有自謂子爲父死臣爲
君死者有自贊孔曰成仁孟曰取義者
均之爲節義也然又有超世遠俗不受
孝廉之舉博學髙尚不仕僞宋之朝者
何生死異道而節義同歸歟有文章名
世一振五代之衰者有淵源典誥自任
===
經濟之業者有見其詩文而稱爲獨立
萬物之表者有讀其封事而稱爲中興
奏疏第一者有本原六經而斟酌司馬
遷韓愈者有見聖人之藴而立言法孟
軻揚雄者是均之以文章名也而亦有
優劣歟且稽古者固有因仍之言論人
者貴有不眩之見然則是數子將何取
歟豈數子之外更有可稱者歟夫道學
昔難其人今誦孔孟而法程朱者比屋
punctuated: 留十五年不屈，而其子亦以節顯者；有被執死于越城，而其孫亦以死著者；有抱印登城，而死戰報國者；有賁卜肆，而慟哭以卒者；有自謂「子爲父死，臣爲君死」者；有自贊「孔曰成仁，孟曰取義」者：均之爲節義也。然又有超世遠俗，不受孝廉之舉，博學髙尚，不仕僞宋之朝者，何生死異道，而節義同歸歟？有文章名世，一振五代之衰者；有淵源典誥，自任經濟之業者；有見其詩文，而稱爲獨立萬物之表者；有讀其封事，而稱爲中興奏疏第一者；有本原六經，而斟酌司馬遷、韓愈者；有見聖人之藴，而立言法孟軻、揚雄者：是均之以文章名也，而亦有優劣歟？且稽古者固有因仍之言，論人者貴有不眩之見。然則是數子將何取歟？豈數子之外，更有可稱者歟？夫道學昔難其人，今誦孔孟而法程朱者比屋
translation_en:
…who was detained for fifteen years without yielding, and whose son likewise became renowned for integrity; there was one who was taken captive and died at Yuecheng, and whose grandson likewise became renowned through his death; one who carried his official seal up onto the city wall and repaid his country by fighting to the death; one who graced a diviner’s stall [?] and died in bitter lamentation; one who declared of himself, “A son dies for his father; a subject dies for his ruler”; and one who wrote in praise of himself, “Confucius spoke of achieving benevolence; Mencius spoke of attaining righteousness.” All alike exemplified integrity and righteousness. Yet there were also those who rose above the world and distanced themselves from vulgar ways, refusing nomination as Filial and Incorrupt, or who, broadly learned and lofty in conduct, would not serve at the court of the illegitimate Song. Why did their different paths of living and dying lead alike to integrity and righteousness?

There was one whose literary writings won renown in his age and at a stroke reversed the decline of the Five Dynasties; one whose writing drew deeply upon the Canons and Counsels, and who took the work of ordering the state and aiding the people as his own responsibility; one whose poetry and prose prompted readers to say that he stood alone beyond all things; one whose sealed memorial prompted readers to rank it foremost among the memorials of the dynastic restoration; one who took the Six Classics as his foundation and judiciously drew upon Sima Qian and Han Yu; and one who perceived the sages’ profound meaning and modeled his writing upon Meng Ke and Yang Xiong. All alike were renowned for their literary writings; yet were there also differences of superiority and inferiority among them? Those who examine antiquity certainly have inherited judgments to draw upon, but those who assess individuals must prize clear, undeluded discernment. What, then, should we admire in these several men? Might there be others beyond them who also deserve praise? In the past, men who embodied the Learning of the Way were hard to find; today, those who recite Confucius and Mencius and model themselves upon the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi are found in household after household…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
皆爾矣何難于古而盛於今歟然自今
觀之民俗日漓士習日下節義之可稱
或寡也豈道學之易而節義之難乎昔
人又謂文章爲末技而秦漢之後作者
亦鮮矣間有稱者不過擅名當代而終
劣前人則文章之難較之道學節義殆
有甚乎諸子誦道學之言懐節義之行
而播之文章燁然可觀也其必有以辯
此幸詳擇而須言之
punctuated: 皆爾矣。何難于古而盛於今歟？然自今觀之，民俗日漓，士習日下，節義之可稱或寡也，豈道學之易而節義之難乎？昔人又謂文章爲末技，而秦漢之後，作者亦鮮矣。間有稱者，不過擅名當代而終劣前人，則文章之難，較之道學節義，殆有甚乎？諸子誦道學之言，懐節義之行，而播之文章，燁然可觀也。其必有以辯此，幸詳擇而須言之。
translation_en: …are all like this. Why was it difficult in antiquity, yet so flourishing today? Yet, judging by present conditions, popular customs grow daily more shallow, and the habits of scholars daily decline; instances of integrity and righteousness worthy of praise are perhaps few. Can it be that Learning of the Way is easy, while integrity and righteousness are difficult? People of former times also called literary composition a minor skill, yet since the Qin and Han dynasties accomplished writers have likewise been rare. Those occasionally praised have merely enjoyed distinction in their own age, remaining inferior to their predecessors. Might the difficulty of literary composition, then, exceed even that of Learning of the Way and of integrity and righteousness? You gentlemen recite the teachings of Learning of the Way, cherish conduct marked by integrity and righteousness, and express these in writing of conspicuous brilliance. Surely you have the means to distinguish among these matters. Please weigh them carefully and set forth your views [?].

中式舉人九十五名。

第一名謝應嶽，吉水縣學增廣生，易。第二名萬敏，南昌縣儒士，書。第三名劉伯躍，南昌府學增廣生，詩。第四名鄧秀，餘干縣學生，春秋。第五名張珩，南昌縣學增廣生，禮記。第六名尹一仁，安福縣學附學生，易。第七名葉尚浩，貴溪縣學附學生，書。第八名吳璁，撫州府學生，詩。第九名王材，新城縣學增廣生，易。第十名錢衡，臨江府學生，詩。第十一名蕭鳴邦，清江縣學生，易。第十二名周弘範，廣永豐縣學附學生，書。第十三名朱憲章，進賢縣學生，詩。第十四名張朝錫，南昌縣學增廣生，易。第十五名傅重祥，進賢縣學附學生，書。第十六名廖暹，瑞州府學生，春秋。
translation_en:
Ninety-five successful provincial graduates (juren).

First: Xie Yingyue, an added student at the Jishui County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

Second: Wan Min, a Confucian scholar from Nanchang County. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.

Third: Liu Boyue, an added student at the Nanchang Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.

Fourth: Deng Xiu, a student at the Yugan County School. His examination classic was the Spring and Autumn Annals.

Fifth: Zhang Heng, an added student at the Nanchang County School. His examination classic was the Book of Rites.

Sixth: Yin Yiren, an attached student at the Anfu County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

Seventh: Ye Shanghao, an attached student at the Guixi County School. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.

Eighth: Wu Cong, a student at the Fuzhou Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.

Ninth: Wang Cai, an added student at the Xincheng County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

Tenth: Qian Heng, a student at the Linjiang Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.

Eleventh: Xiao Mingbang, a student at the Qingjiang County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

Twelfth: Zhou Hongfan, an attached student at the Yongfeng County School in Guangxin Prefecture (abbreviated as Guang in the text). His examination classic was the Book of Documents.

Thirteenth: Zhu Xianzhang, a student at the Jinxian County School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.

Fourteenth: Zhang Chaoxi, an added student at the Nanchang County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

Fifteenth: Fu Chongxiang, an attached student at the Jinxian County School. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.

Sixteenth: Liao Xian, a student at the Ruizhou Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Spring and Autumn Annals.

聖人告大夫盡道於己則所欲於民者無不得

聖人告大夫，盡道於己，則所欲於民者無不得焉。夫從道而不從欲者，民也。苟能自盡其所當盡，民其有弗應矣乎？季康子問使民敬忠以勸，而夫子告之如此。盖謂上下有分，感應有機。民之未盡其道，亦求諸己而已。是故民不作敬，無但曰民敢慢也，其或啓之有自，而容貌之動不

Four Books

“Preside over them with dignity, and they will be respectful; be filial and compassionate, and they will be loyal; promote the good and teach those who lack ability, and they will be encouraged to exert themselves.”

Yin Yiren

Associate Examiner Hu, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The exposition of principle is unhurried and ample, and its conception lofty and imbued with antiquity. It is more than merely a model for contemporary examination prose.〕
Associate Examiner Ren, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The style is elegant and restrained, capable of reforming the prevailing habits of superficiality. Select it for inclusion.〕
Associate Examiner Zhu, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔It captures precisely the sage’s meaning in his words to Kangzi.〕
Examiner Tu, Secretary, comments: 〔This should not be regarded as merely a contemporary examination essay on the Classics.〕
Examiner Lu, Acting Director, comments: 〔Subtle in expression, yet conforming to proper standards.〕

The sage told the grand master that, if he fully realized the Way in his own conduct, there would be nothing he desired of the people that he could not obtain. For the people follow the Way, not another’s desires. If one fully discharges all that one ought to discharge, could the people fail to respond? Ji Kangzi asked how to make the people respectful and loyal and encourage them to exert themselves, and the Master answered him in these terms. His meaning was that superiors and inferiors have their distinct stations, and that influence and response have their workings. 驕而爲顯若之觀則民見其難說而難犯也望
之而畏必生即之而急必息皆將欽翼以事其
上矣奚待使之而後敬耶民不作忠無但曰民
敢倍也其或導之無本而孝慈之道未兼舉乎
必也立愛惟親而大倫之克盡保民如子而苛
政之不施則民見其可愛而可慕也協德而心
罔弗盡好義而事必有終皆將貞一以戴其上
矣奚待使之而後忠耶以至民不作勸亦無但
===
曰民敢懈也旌別之未當誘掖之未至或有之
矣又必於善者舉之而恒以蔽賢爲懼不能者
教之而每以棄才爲惜則見嘉善矜愚之政行
而自畫自棄之民化感知遇之難也益相奮勵
而進善於無窮荷甄陶之德也更相飭戒而遷
善之無已亦奚待夫上之使而後勸哉是則康
子所問皆欲以責之民夫子答之皆欲其反之
已感應之道不外是矣雖然夫子之言非專爲
康子告也康子以陪臣柄魯魯之民豈康子所
punctuated: 以禮乎？必也涖官有則，而著儼然之威；居上不驕，而爲顯若之觀。則民見其難說而難犯也，望之而畏必生，即之而急必息，皆將欽翼以事其上矣，奚待使之而後敬耶？民不作忠，無但曰民敢倍也，其或導之無本，而孝慈之道未兼舉乎？必也立愛惟親，而大倫之克盡；保民如子，而苛政之不施。則民見其可愛而可慕也，協德而心罔弗盡，好義而事必有終，皆將貞一以戴其上矣，奚待使之而後忠耶？以至民不作勸，亦無但曰民敢懈也。旌別之未當，誘掖之未至，或有之矣。又必於善者舉之，而恒以蔽賢爲懼；不能者教之，而每以棄才爲惜。則見嘉善矜愚之政行，而自畫自棄之民化。感知遇之難也，益相奮勵，而進善於無窮；荷甄陶之德也，更相飭戒，而遷善之無已。亦奚待夫上之使而後勸哉？是則康子所問，皆欲以責之民；夫子答之，皆欲其反之已。感應之道，不外是矣。雖然，夫子之言，非專爲康子告也。康子以陪臣柄魯，魯之民豈康子所
translation_en:
…in accordance with ritual propriety? He must observe proper standards in administering his office and display a solemn dignity; he must occupy his superior position without arrogance and present a visibly impressive bearing. The people will then see that he is difficult to please and difficult to offend. Looking upon him, they will inevitably feel awe; approaching him, their agitation will inevitably subside. All will serve their superior with reverent care. Why should they need to be commanded before showing respect?

If the people fail to show loyalty, do not merely say that they dare to betray their superior. Might his guidance lack a foundation, and might he have failed to practice both filial devotion and parental kindness? He must establish affection first toward his parents and fully discharge the great familial relationships; he must protect the people as his own children and refrain from oppressive government. The people will then see that he is worthy of love and admiration. They will unite with him in virtue and devote their hearts without reserve; they will cherish righteousness and carry their undertakings through to completion. All will uphold their superior with steadfast, undivided allegiance. Why should they need to be commanded before showing loyalty?

And if the people fail to exert themselves, likewise do not merely say that they dare to be idle. Perhaps he has not properly distinguished the deserving, or has not sufficiently encouraged and assisted them. He must promote the good, always fearing that he might obscure the worthy; he must teach those who lack ability, always regretting any waste of talent. Then, as policies that commend the good and show solicitude for the ignorant take effect, those who set limits upon themselves or abandon themselves will be transformed. Appreciating how rare it is to have their worth recognized, they will increasingly encourage one another and advance endlessly in goodness. Grateful for the beneficence that cultivates and molds them, they will admonish one another and turn toward goodness without cease. Why should they need commands from above before exerting themselves?

Thus, everything Kangzi asked concerned demands he wished to impose upon the people; everything the Master said in reply sought to make him turn those demands back upon himself. The way of influence and response goes no further than this. Nevertheless, the Master's words were not addressed exclusively to Kangzi. Kangzi wielded power in Lu as a subordinate minister. How could the people of Lu be Kangzi's to…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
得而有哉非其有而有之民不敬忠且勸固其
宜耳夫子嘗曰斯民也三代之所以直道而行
也不於此而益驗歟孔氏疏乃謂執政如君故
盡告以人君之事不知夫子之言非專爲康子
告也雖然亦衰世之意也未敬施而民敬未施
信而民信不待賞而民勸三代之盛固如此
舜好問而好察邇言隱惡而揚善執其兩
端用其中於民
夏寶
===
同考試官教諭曾　批〔簡古〕
同考試官教諭何　批〔迥異衆作〕
考試官主事曆　批〔甚精〕
考試官署郎中盧　批〔古雅〕
聖人大知之實無非樂取人以爲善也夫知不
在於自用而善貴乎兼天下也聖人慱求乎善
而精擇以行之其樂取諸人何如哉中庸引夫
子之稱舜以見道之所以行也謂夫世之以知
稱者恒自滿而拒人則其爲知也亦小矣舜之
punctuated:
得而有哉？非其有而有之，民不敬忠且勸，固其宜耳。夫子嘗曰：「斯民也，三代之所以直道而行也。」不於此而益驗歟？孔氏疏乃謂執政如君，故盡告以人君之事，不知夫子之言非專爲康子告也。雖然，亦衰世之意也。未敬施而民敬，未施信而民信，不待賞而民勸，三代之盛固如此。
舜好問而好察邇言，隱惡而揚善，執其兩端，用其中於民。
夏寶
同考試官教諭曾，批〔簡古〕。
同考試官教諭何，批〔迥異衆作〕。
考試官主事曆，批〔甚精〕。
考試官署郎中盧，批〔古雅〕。
聖人大知之實，無非樂取人以爲善也。夫知不在於自用，而善貴乎兼天下也。聖人慱求乎善，而精擇以行之，其樂取諸人何如哉！中庸引夫子之稱舜，以見道之所以行也。謂夫世之以知稱者，恒自滿而拒人，則其爲知也亦小矣。舜之
translation_en:
…could he rightfully possess them? He possessed what was not his to possess; it was only fitting that the people should fail to be respectful, loyal, and zealous. The Master once said: “These people are those through whom the Three Dynasties proceeded along the straight Way.” Is this not further borne out here? Yet Kong’s subcommentary says that one who administers government is like a ruler, and therefore the Master instructed him fully in the affairs of a sovereign. It fails to recognize that the Master’s words were not addressed exclusively to Kangzi. Even so, these words also reflect an age of decline. Before respect is shown [?], the people are respectful; before trustworthiness is displayed, the people are trusting; without awaiting rewards, the people exert themselves. Such indeed was the flourishing condition of the Three Dynasties.
“Shun delighted in asking questions and examining ordinary words. He concealed what was bad and made known what was good. He grasped the two extremes and applied the mean between them to the people.”
Xia Bao
Associate Examiner Zeng, an Instructor, commented: “Concise and archaic.”
Associate Examiner He, an Instructor, commented: “Strikingly different from the other compositions.”
Examiner Li [?], a Secretary, commented: “Very refined.”
Examiner Lu, an acting Director, commented: “Classical and elegant.”
The substance of the sage’s great wisdom consists entirely in his delight in drawing upon others to do good. Wisdom does not lie in relying solely upon oneself, while the value of goodness lies in embracing all under Heaven. The sage seeks goodness widely [?] and selects carefully from it to put it into practice: how great is his delight in drawing upon others! The Doctrine of the Mean quotes the Master’s praise of Shun to show how the Way is put into practice. Those in the world who are celebrated for wisdom are constantly self-satisfied and reject others; their wisdom is thus petty indeed. As for Shun’s…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
所謂大知者何哉夫人未知則有問舜之聖本
生知則有不待問者而况於好問耶猶以爲理
無不在而智識有限或局焉而不周也故求言
之念恒切於中而下問之勞弗自知矣允理雖
明則有察問焉而得邇言則固不待察者而况
於好察耶舜以爲言無可畧而常道所寓或槩
焉以有遺也故邇言所聞必求諸道而言之遠
者察可知矣然天下之理貞夫一而事有是非
言之在人不能無善惡也于其惡者而隱之無
===
稽雖嚴於弗用而聞諸我者不以彰之人也人
豈有所愧而弗以告哉于其善者而揚之嘉謨
有取于周咨則知之獨者必欲公諸人也人其
無所勸而弗自盡哉然天下之事有不同而中
無定在言之善者又不能無兩端也則即夫衆
論之異而折以吾心之公善無常主必精擇而
要其歸焉務見夫大中之極致而過與不及者
在所舍耳由是得夫至一之理而快其從善之
心用人惟己必果決以致諸行焉蓋能通天下
punctuated: 所謂大知者何哉？夫人未知則有問，舜之聖本生知，則有不待問者，而况於好問耶？猶以爲理無不在，而智識有限，或局焉而不周也。故求言之念恒切於中，而下問之勞弗自知矣。允理雖明則有察，問焉而得邇言，則固不待察者，而况於好察耶？舜以爲言無可畧，而常道所寓，或槩焉以有遺也。故邇言所聞，必求諸道，而言之遠者，察可知矣。然天下之理貞夫一，而事有是非，言之在人不能無善惡也。于其惡者而隱之，無稽雖嚴於弗用，而聞諸我者不以彰之人也。人豈有所愧而弗以告哉？于其善者而揚之，嘉謨有取于周咨，則知之獨者必欲公諸人也。人其無所勸而弗自盡哉？然天下之事有不同，而中無定在，言之善者又不能無兩端也。則即夫衆論之異，而折以吾心之公，善無常主，必精擇而要其歸焉。務見夫大中之極致，而過與不及者在所舍耳。由是得夫至一之理，而快其從善之心，用人惟己，必果決以致諸行焉。蓋能通天下
translation_en:
…what was meant by his great wisdom? People ask questions when they do not know something. Shun, being a sage, possessed knowledge from birth; there were thus things he did not need to ask about. How much more remarkable, then, that he delighted in asking questions! He still considered that principle was present everywhere, while knowledge and understanding were limited and might be confined rather than comprehensive. Thus the desire to seek others’ counsel was always urgent within him, and he was himself unaware of the toil of consulting those below him. Even when true principle was clear, there was still examination to undertake [?]; ordinary remarks obtained through questioning would seemingly require no examination. How much more remarkable, then, that he delighted in examining them! Shun considered that no words could be disregarded: where the constant Way resided, something might be missed through sweeping generalization. Thus, whenever he heard ordinary remarks, he invariably sought the Way in them; one can readily understand how he examined words of more far-reaching significance.

Yet the principles of all under Heaven converge upon unity, while affairs admit of right and wrong, and people’s words inevitably contain both good and bad. He concealed what was bad. Although he firmly refused to put groundless statements into practice, he did not expose to others what he himself had heard. How, then, could people feel ashamed and refrain from telling him things? He publicized what was good. When he found sound counsel through wide consultation, he invariably wished to share with others what he alone had learned. How could people fail to be encouraged and to express themselves fully?

Yet affairs throughout the world differ, and the mean has no fixed position; even good counsel inevitably presents opposing extremes. He therefore took the differences among the many opinions and judged them with the impartiality of his own mind. Goodness had no fixed proprietor: he had to choose with discrimination and seek the point toward which these opinions converged. He strove to discern the utmost realization of the great mean, discarding excess and deficiency. In this way he apprehended the principle of ultimate unity and satisfied his heart’s desire to follow goodness. Taking others’ strengths as his own, he invariably acted decisively to put them into practice. For he was able to unite all under Heaven…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
爲一身而不自滿假者固如是耳夫自耕稼陶
漁以至爲帝而與善之心無間雖匹夫匹婦皆
獲自盡而協一之功有成此舜之知異乎知愚
者之過不及而道所以行也抑論性無不具故
人已之善一也合內外之道也舜之善與人同
者有見于此耳二則異異則私私則人已隔而
內外離善不可爲矣故道之不行也皆二之之
弊也堯之稽衆禹之拜昌言文王之不聞亦式
不諫亦入皆此道也后之學聖人者如之何一
===
夫人已其幾矣
萬物皆備於我矣反身而誠樂莫大焉强
恕而行求仁莫近焉
朱憲章
同考試官教諭羅　批〔詞不費而意自完必理學〕
有得者
同考試官教諭沈　批〔純實〕
考試官主事屠　批〔爾雅〕
考試官署郎中盧　批〔意足〕
punctuated:
爲一身而不自滿假者，固如是耳。夫自耕稼陶漁以至爲帝，而與善之心無間，雖匹夫匹婦皆獲自盡，而協一之功有成。此舜之知異乎知愚者之過不及，而道所以行也。抑論性無不具，故人已之善一也，合內外之道也。舜之善與人同者，有見于此耳。二則異，異則私，私則人已隔而內外離，善不可爲矣。故道之不行也，皆二之之弊也。堯之稽衆，禹之拜昌言，文王之不聞亦式、不諫亦入，皆此道也。后之學聖人者如之何？一夫人已，其幾矣。

萬物皆備於我矣。反身而誠，樂莫大焉；强恕而行，求仁莫近焉。

朱憲章

同考試官教諭羅，批〔詞不費而意自完，必理學〕有得者。

同考試官教諭沈，批〔純實〕

考試官主事屠，批〔爾雅〕

考試官署郎中盧，批〔意足〕
translation_en:
…into a single body without becoming complacent or presumptuous: this is indeed how he acted. From his days of farming, making pottery, and fishing until he became emperor, his readiness to join others in goodness never faltered. Even ordinary men and women could fully contribute their abilities, and thus his work of bringing all into harmony and unity succeeded. This is how Shun’s wisdom differed from the excesses of the clever and the shortcomings of the foolish, and why the Way was put into practice.

Moreover, human nature lacks nothing; hence the goodness of others and that of oneself are one. This is the Way that unites the inner and the outer. Shun shared goodness with others because he understood this. To treat them as two is to make them different; difference leads to selfishness; selfishness separates others from oneself and divides the inner from the outer, making goodness impossible to realize. Thus, whenever the Way fails to prevail, the fault lies in treating these as two. Yao’s consulting the multitude, Yu’s bowing before excellent counsel, and King Wen’s following the right pattern even without instruction and accepting what was right even without remonstrance—all exemplify this Way. What should later students of the sages do? Unite others and oneself, and they will come close.

“All things are complete within me. To turn inward and find oneself sincere—there is no greater joy. To act with strenuous attention to reciprocity—there is no nearer way to seek benevolence.”

Zhu Xianzhang

Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “The wording is economical, yet the meaning is complete in itself. Surely the author has attained an understanding of the learning of principle.”

Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor, comments: “Pure and substantial.”

Examiner Tu, Secretary, comments: “Refined and correct.”

Examiner Lu, Acting Director, comments: “The meaning is fully expressed.”

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
大賢論人全具乎衆理已純而樂有餘未純而
求有術夫人之所以爲人以其有是理也其純
者固有餘樂矣未純而力行以求之理豈遠乎
哉孟子之意蓋謂理之大原出於天而其實體
存乎人故盈天地之間何者非物何者非理何
者非吾之所備哉有物有則彝倫叙于相協之
初與生俱生恒性全于降衷之始語大天下莫
能載語小天下莫能破而此身不見其不足也
以言乎遠則不禦以言乎邇則靜而正而此身
===
不見其或遺也夫理無不備則所任亦重矣然
豈能人人盡無私欲之間哉必於所備之理反
之躬行果皆眞實而無怍於人察之日用初非
矯飾而有疚於内則是付之本全存之不失所
如皆利無自欺而有自慊樂以天矣樂有大於
此乎此仁之事理之純也未至此者又必於所
備之理黽勉以從事推己及物而不梏於自私
公溥以爲心能近取譬而必期於無我則是失
之未遠求之有益所欲皆遂本在内而非在外
punctuated:
大賢論人全具乎衆理，已純而樂有餘，未純而求有術。夫人之所以爲人，以其有是理也。其純者固有餘樂矣，未純而力行以求之，理豈遠乎哉？孟子之意，蓋謂理之大原出於天，而其實體存乎人。故盈天地之間，何者非物？何者非理？何者非吾之所備哉？有物有則，彝倫叙于相協之初；與生俱生，恒性全于降衷之始。語大，天下莫能載；語小，天下莫能破，而此身不見其不足也。以言乎遠，則不禦；以言乎邇，則靜而正，而此身不見其或遺也。

夫理無不備，則所任亦重矣。然豈能人人盡無私欲之間哉？必於所備之理，反之躬行，果皆眞實而無怍於人；察之日用，初非矯飾而有疚於内。則是付之本全，存之不失，所如皆利，無自欺而有自慊，樂以天矣。樂有大於此乎？此仁之事，理之純也。

未至此者，又必於所備之理，黽勉以從事，推己及物而不梏於自私，公溥以爲心，能近取譬而必期於無我。則是失之未遠，求之有益，所欲皆遂，本在内而非在外。
translation_en:
The great worthy explains that human beings are fully endowed with all principles: when these are already pure, joy abounds; when they are not yet pure, there is a method for seeking them. What makes human beings human is their possession of these principles. Those in whom they are pure certainly have abundant joy. For those in whom they are not yet pure, but who earnestly put them into practice in order to seek them, could principle be far away? Mengzi’s meaning is surely that the great source of principle issues from Heaven, while its actual substance resides in human beings. Thus, among all that fills heaven and earth, what is not a thing? What is without principle? What is not already fully present in me? Wherever there are things, there are their norms: the constant human relationships were ordered at the very inception of mutual concord [?]. Born together with life itself, our constant nature was complete from the moment Heaven bestowed our inner moral constitution. Speaking of its greatness, nothing under Heaven can contain it; speaking of its smallness, nothing under Heaven can divide it. Yet in this person it is found in no way deficient. Speaking of its reach, nothing can restrain it; speaking of its nearness, it is still and correct. Yet in this person nothing of it is found to be missing.

Since no principle is absent from us, the responsibility we bear is also weighty. Yet how could everyone be entirely free from the intrusion of selfish desires? We must return to the principles with which we are endowed and examine them in our own conduct: are they all truly realized, leaving us without shame before others? We must scrutinize them in everyday practice: is our conduct free from contrivance and pretense that would leave us inwardly uneasy? Then what was originally bestowed in its completeness is preserved without loss; wherever we turn, all goes well. There is no self-deception, but rather inward contentment, and our joy accords with Heaven. Could any joy be greater than this? This is the work of benevolence and the purity of principle.

Those who have not yet reached this must diligently apply themselves to the principles with which they are endowed, extending consideration from themselves to other beings without being fettered by selfishness. They must make impartiality and all-embracing concern their disposition, drawing analogies from what lies close at hand—themselves—and aiming resolutely at freedom from self-centeredness. Then they have not strayed far from what they have lost, and seeking it brings benefit. All that they desire is fulfilled; its root lies within, not outside …

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
仁斯至矣仁豈難於復乎孟子之論如此以見
理初不外乎人人皆可勉而至學者其亦加強
恕之功以驗誠身之樂哉雖然此非孟子之言
也孟子子思曾子相授受而得之孔子者也孔
子曰誠者天之道也誠之者人之道也反身而
誠誠者矣然亦誠之者之自然處也强恕而行
誠之者矣然亦誠者之勉然時也誠者誠之者
寧復有二道哉後世謂聖本生知非學可至則
於反身而誠者固已擬之爲絕德矣噫視人則
擬爲絕德自視則甘爲下愚不亦惑乎不亦惑
乎
===
易
乾道變化各正性命保合大和乃利貞
同考試官訓導胡　批〔性理之學至難言也此作發揮題意明盡非深於理者不能〕
同考試官訓導任　批〔變化二字場中多以化漸變成牽合成文可厭援出理氣僅見此篇錄之〕
punctuated:
仁斯至矣，仁豈難於復乎？孟子之論如此，以見理初不外乎人，人人皆可勉而至。學者其亦加强恕之功，以驗誠身之樂哉！雖然，此非孟子之言也，孟子、子思、曾子相授受而得之孔子者也。孔子曰：「誠者，天之道也；誠之者，人之道也。」反身而誠，誠者矣，然亦誠之者之自然處也；强恕而行，誠之者矣，然亦誠者之勉然時也。誠者、誠之者，寧復有二道哉？後世謂聖本生知，非學可至，則於反身而誠者，固已擬之爲絕德矣。噫！視人則擬爲絕德，自視則甘爲下愚，不亦惑乎？不亦惑乎？

易

乾道變化，各正性命，保合大和，乃利貞。

同考試官訓導胡　批〔性理之學至難言也，此作發揮題意明盡，非深於理者不能。〕

同考試官訓導任　批〔變化二字，場中多以化漸變成牽合成文，可厭。援出理氣，僅見此篇，錄之。〕
translation_en:
…Benevolence then arrives. How could benevolence be difficult to recover? Mencius argues thus to show that principle is never external to human beings, and that everyone can attain it through effort. Should not students also intensify their efforts at sympathetic understanding, so as to experience the joy of making themselves sincere? Yet these are not words originating with Mencius alone: Mencius, Zisi, and Zengzi transmitted and received this teaching in succession, deriving it from Confucius. Confucius said: “Sincerity is the Way of Heaven; making oneself sincere is the Way of human beings.” To turn inward and find oneself sincere is to possess sincerity; yet it is also the state of spontaneity reached by one who strives to become sincere. To act with diligent sympathetic understanding is to strive to become sincere; yet it is also the moment of exertion for one who possesses sincerity. Could possessing sincerity and striving to become sincere really constitute two different Ways? Later generations say that sages are born knowing, and that their attainment cannot be reached through learning. They thus already regard those who turn inward and find themselves sincere as possessing an unattainable virtue. Alas! In viewing others, they deem their virtue unattainable; in viewing themselves, they willingly remain among the lowest fools. Is this not delusion? Is this not delusion?

Book of Changes

“The Way of Qian transforms and changes; each thing thereby receives its proper nature and allotted destiny. Preserving and uniting in great harmony, it is thus beneficial and steadfast.”

Associate Examiner Hu, an Assistant Instructor, comments: “The learning of human nature and principle is exceedingly difficult to discuss. This composition develops the meaning of the topic clearly and fully; only someone with a profound understanding of principle could accomplish this.”

Associate Examiner Ren, an Assistant Instructor, comments: “For the two words ‘transformation’ and ‘change,’ many candidates in this examination have forced together the notions that transformation is gradual and change is its completion to construct their essays—most tiresome. This is the only essay I have seen that brings out principle and material force. I have selected it for inclusion.”

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導祝　批〔詞約而理盡殆深於易者〕
考試官主事屠　批〔是知乾義者〕
考試官署郎中盧　批〔變化處點出理氣利貞後補出〕
〔起元意此作備知之〕
彖傳即天道運而物理全而著其爲利貞也蓋
物至於各正保合則得其理以自全而利貞之
實在是矣天道之運之妙爲何如哉夫子彖乾
以天道明之及此蓋謂乾之利貞不可見亦於
天之造物者驗之焉是故於穆不已天道乃一
===
理之流行耳而氣實承之其流行者變化也有
先後焉而無端也乎以槖籥乎群生絪緼無間
天道乃一氣之往來耳而理實主之其往來者
變化也有遲速焉而不息也乎以陶鎔乎庶彙
但見物始於元而通於亨莫不有性命焉然理
之方行未足謂之各正也今則於其萬殊之中
而有一定之則渾全完具至大而非有餘至小
而非不足也凡賦受之所具者至此各正而氣
固無不行矣亦莫不有大和焉然氣之方出未
punctuated:
同考試官訓導祝批〔詞約而理盡，殆深於易者。〕
考試官主事屠批〔是知乾義者。〕
考試官署郎中盧批〔變化處點出理氣，利貞後補出〕〔起元意，此作備知之。〕
彖傳即天道運而物理全，而著其爲利貞也。蓋物至於各正保合，則得其理以自全，而利貞之實在是矣。天道之運之妙爲何如哉？夫子彖乾，以天道明之，及此蓋謂乾之利貞不可見，亦於天之造物者驗之焉。是故於穆不已，天道乃一理之流行耳，而氣實承之。其流行者變化也，有先後焉，而無端也乎？以槖籥乎群生。絪緼無間，天道乃一氣之往來耳，而理實主之。其往來者變化也，有遲速焉，而不息也乎？以陶鎔乎庶彙。但見物始於元而通於亨，莫不有性命焉。然理之方行，未足謂之各正也。今則於其萬殊之中，而有一定之則，渾全完具，至大而非有餘，至小而非不足也。凡賦受之所具者，至此各正，而氣固無不行矣。亦莫不有大和焉，然氣之方出未
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zhu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The wording is concise, yet the principles are fully expressed. This is surely someone deeply versed in the Book of Changes.”
Examiner Tu, Secretary, comments: “This is someone who understands the meaning of Qian.”
Examiner Lu, Acting Director, comments: “At ‘change and transformation,’ the essay brings out principle and material force; after ‘beneficial steadfastness,’ it supplies” “the idea of initiating the origination anew. This essay shows a thorough understanding of these matters.”
The Commentary on the Judgments considers the movement of the Way of Heaven and the completeness of the principles of things, thereby revealing what constitutes ‘beneficial steadfastness.’ For when things reach the point where each attains its proper nature and allotted destiny, and preserves and unites its supreme harmony, they obtain their principles and thereby complete themselves. Herein lies the substance of beneficial steadfastness. How wondrous is the operation of the Way of Heaven! In his judgment on Qian, the Master elucidates it through the Way of Heaven. At this point, he presumably means that Qian’s beneficial steadfastness cannot itself be seen, but can nevertheless be verified through Heaven’s creation of things. Thus, profound and unceasing, the Way of Heaven is simply the flowing operation of a single principle, which material force actually bears. This flowing operation is change and transformation: it has succession, yet has no beginning, does it not? Through it, Heaven acts as a bellows upon all living beings. Intermingling without interruption, the Way of Heaven is simply the coming and going of a single material force, which principle actually governs. This coming and going is change and transformation: it has differences of speed, yet never ceases, does it not? Through it, Heaven molds and casts the myriad kinds of beings.
We see that things begin in origination and develop freely through flourishing; none lacks its nature and allotted destiny. Yet while principle is still unfolding, one cannot adequately say that each has attained its proper condition. Now, amid their myriad differences, each has a fixed standard, wholly complete and fully equipped: the greatest has no excess, and the smallest has no deficiency. Everything comprised in what Heaven bestows and things receive now attains its proper condition, and material force assuredly operates everywhere. Nor does anything lack supreme harmony. Yet while material force is still emerging, it has not yet …

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
是謂之保合也今則於其發育之際而有機緘
之妙冲融會萃旋之而益固斂之而益密也凡
眞精之所凝者至此保合而理自無不寓矣是
蓋闢矣而闔用藏於仁之既顯而靜中之動固
已伏於其間通矣而復法效於象之已成而寂
中之感固已兆於其時矣謂之曰乃利貞者其
所以終乎元亨之始而天運循環之妙不於是
而可見哉彖傳發明乾義至矣抑乾之道天道
也君道也乾有四德天有四時人君則順四時
===
以行四德如八柄之馭月令之布典禮之勑無
非奉若之而已矣文言曰君子行此四德者故
曰乾元亨利貞蓋即以君子當乾而至德惟至
健者能行也先儒謂君德以剛爲主其有以識
此夫
是故法象莫大乎天地變通莫大乎四時
縣象著明莫大乎日月崇高莫大乎富
貴備物致用立成器以爲天下利莫大
乎聖人探賾索隱鉤深致遠以定天下
punctuated:
是謂之保合也。今則於其發育之際，而有機緘之妙，冲融會萃，旋之而益固，斂之而益密也。凡眞精之所凝者，至此保合，而理自無不寓矣。是蓋闢矣而闔，用藏於仁之既顯，而靜中之動固已伏於其間；通矣而復，法效於象之已成，而寂中之感固已兆於其時矣。謂之曰「乃利貞」者，其所以終乎元亨之始，而天運循環之妙，不於是而可見哉？《彖傳》發明乾義至矣。抑乾之道，天道也，君道也。乾有四德，天有四時，人君則順四時以行四德，如八柄之馭、月令之布、典禮之勑，無非奉若之而已矣。《文言》曰：「君子行此四德者，故曰乾元亨利貞。」蓋即以君子當乾，而至德惟至健者能行也。先儒謂君德以剛爲主，其有以識此夫！

是故法象莫大乎天地，變通莫大乎四時，縣象著明莫大乎日月，崇高莫大乎富貴，備物致用、立成器以爲天下利莫大乎聖人，探賾索隱、鉤深致遠，以定天下
translation_en:
…be called preservation in union [?]. Now, amid their development and growth, there is the marvel of a hidden mechanism: harmoniously blending and converging, they become firmer as they revolve and more closely knit as they draw inward. Whatever the true essence has congealed into is, at this point, preserved in union, and principle is naturally present everywhere within it. Thus, opening gives way to closing: functioning is stored away after benevolence has become manifest, while movement within stillness already lies concealed therein. Free passage gives way to return: patterns take effect in forms already completed, while responsiveness within quiescence has already shown its first signs at that moment. The words “thus, beneficial and steadfast” describe how the beginning made by origination and flourishing is brought to completion. Is it not here that the marvel of Heaven’s cyclical operation can be seen? The Commentary on the Judgments expounds the meaning of Qian to the fullest.

Yet the Way of Qian is both the Way of Heaven and the Way of the ruler. Qian has four virtues, and Heaven has four seasons; the ruler follows the four seasons in putting the four virtues into practice. Governing through the eight handles of authority, promulgating the Monthly Ordinances, and setting forth statutes and rites—all these are simply ways of reverently following it. The Commentary on the Words of the Text says: “The gentleman practices these four virtues; therefore it is said: ‘Qian: origination, flourishing, benefit, and steadfastness.’” This directly identifies the gentleman with Qian, for only one of utmost vigor can practice the highest virtue. Earlier Confucian scholars said that firmness is the governing quality of a ruler’s virtue. Surely they had some understanding of this!

Therefore, for patterns and images, nothing is greater than Heaven and Earth; for change and continuity, nothing is greater than the four seasons; for suspended images that shine manifestly, nothing is greater than the sun and moon; for eminence and exaltation, nothing is greater than wealth and noble rank; for providing things for use and establishing finished implements to benefit all under Heaven, none is greater than the sage; for probing the intricate and seeking the hidden, plumbing the depths and reaching afar, in order to determine for all under Heaven…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
之吉凶成天下之亹亹者莫大乎蓍龜
王林
同考試官訓導胡　批〔神物功用必合天人功用以見其大而功用之大又自聖人神之此作說理明盡〕
〔收拾無遺是不越矩度者取之〕
同考試官訓導任　批〔長題收拾殆盡且平易冲澹殊不犯力其學易而有得者歟欽羨〕
同考試官訓導祝　批〔不費繁辭而卜筮之功用百著蓋有得於潔靜精微之旨者〕
考試官主事屠　批〔詞不費而理自足錄之以爲長〕
===
考試官署郎中盧　批〔試錄經義多非士子本文閱卷得此錄之然亦不待潤色矣〕
〔題式〕
大傳欲極言蓍龜之功用必倒以天人之極者
而實之也蓋蓍龜備天人之理而至神者也夫
子傳易而舉凡例以著其極可謂善形容矣且
易有八卦吉凶以定大業乃生然其所以定所
以生則有蓍龜爲之先焉其功用之大自有不
punctuated:
之吉凶，成天下之亹亹者，莫大乎蓍龜。
王林
同考試官訓導胡批〔神物功用，必合天人功用以見其大，而功用之大，又自聖人神之。此作說理明盡〕〔收拾無遺，是不越矩度者，取之。〕
同考試官訓導任批〔長題收拾殆盡，且平易冲澹，殊不犯力，其學易而有得者歟？欽羨。〕

考試官主事屠批〔詞不費而理自足，錄之以爲長。〕
考試官署郎中盧批〔試錄經義多非士子本文，閱卷得此錄之，然亦不待潤色矣。〕
〔題式〕

Wang Lin.

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
可泯者矣是故乾易坤簡天地之灋象也灋象
莫大乎天地焉寒往暑來四時之變通也變通
莫大乎四時焉日明於晝月明於夜著明者莫
大乎日月也富有四海貴為天子崇高者莫大
乎富貴也民資於物而備物以致用用資於器
而立器以利民則是既竭耳目心思之力繼以
灋制品節之詳固惟聖人之能事亦惟聖人之
為大也若乃賾而雜者探之不遺隱而微者索
之使顯鉤夫深而不限於未明致夫遠而不限
===
於未至于以定吉凶而使天下無不斷之疑于
以成亹亹而使天下無不定之業則又莫有大
於蓍龜者蓋其為物也小而其為用也大衍之
以四十有九則物理該括於分揲掛扐之後問
焉以言神之至也匪蓍殆倀倀乎無所之矣鑽
之以七十有二則民故昭晰于雨霽蒙驛克之
兆命焉斯應靈之至也舍龜將貿貿焉無所從
矣是則無蓍龜則無卜筮無卜筮則吉凶隱而
大業隳矣此蓍龜之不可少而功用之大孰有過
punctuated: 可泯者矣。是故乾易坤簡，天地之灋象也，灋象莫大乎天地焉；寒往暑來，四時之變通也，變通莫大乎四時焉；日明於晝，月明於夜，著明者莫大乎日月也；富有四海，貴為天子，崇高者莫大乎富貴也。民資於物，而備物以致用；用資於器，而立器以利民。則是既竭耳目心思之力，繼以灋制品節之詳，固惟聖人之能事，亦惟聖人之為大也。若乃賾而雜者探之不遺，隱而微者索之使顯，鉤夫深而不限於未明，致夫遠而不限於未至，于以定吉凶而使天下無不斷之疑，于以成亹亹而使天下無不定之業，則又莫有大於蓍龜者。蓋其為物也小，而其為用也大。衍之以四十有九，則物理該括於分揲掛扐之後；問焉以言，神之至也，匪蓍殆倀倀乎無所之矣。鑽之以七十有二，則民故昭晰于雨霽蒙驛克之兆；命焉斯應，靈之至也，舍龜將貿貿焉無所從矣。是則無蓍龜則無卜筮，無卜筮則吉凶隱而大業隳矣。此蓍龜之不可少，而功用之大孰有過
translation_en: …cannot be effaced. Thus, the ease of Qian and the simplicity of Kun are the patterns of Heaven and Earth: no patterns are greater than Heaven and Earth. Cold departs and heat arrives—these are the transformations and continuities of the four seasons: none are greater than those of the four seasons. The sun shines by day and the moon by night: among things that shine, none are greater than the sun and moon. To possess the wealth of all within the Four Seas and the exalted rank of the Son of Heaven: among things lofty and eminent, none are greater than wealth and rank. The people depend upon material things, so these are furnished for use; their use depends upon implements, so implements are established to benefit the people. This requires first exhausting the powers of hearing, sight, and thought, then following these with detailed regulations, distinctions, and measured adjustments. Such accomplishments belong to the sage alone, and here too the sage alone is supreme. As for exploring what is intricate and confused without omission, seeking out what is hidden and subtle and bringing it to light, drawing forth what is deep without being confined by what remains obscure, and reaching what is distant without being confined by what has not yet been attained—thereby determining good and ill fortune so that no doubt under Heaven remains unresolved, and bringing sustained endeavors to completion so that no undertaking under Heaven remains unsettled—in these respects nothing is greater than milfoil stalks and tortoise shells. As objects they are small, but their usefulness is great. When the operation is performed with forty-nine stalks, the principles of things are comprehensively embraced through dividing the stalks, counting them in groups, setting one aside, and placing the remainders between the fingers. Address a question to them in words: this is spiritual efficacy at its utmost. Without milfoil, one would surely wander bewildered, with nowhere to turn. When the shell is drilled according to the number seventy-two, human affairs become clearly discernible in the crack configurations called rain, clearing, clouding, dispersal [?], and crossing. Give it a charge and it responds: this is numinous efficacy at its utmost. Without the tortoise shell, one would be utterly at a loss, with nothing to follow. Thus, without milfoil and tortoise shells there would be neither shell nor stalk divination; without divination, good and ill fortune would remain concealed and great undertakings would fall into ruin. This is why milfoil and tortoise shells cannot be dispensed with; and in the greatness of their efficacy and usefulness, what could surpass…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
之者哉抑易爲卜筮作也所以開物成務而利
天下也周禮建大卜筮人之官書建稽疑而卜
筮列五謀之二古者國有大事則必參之人謀
斷以蓍龜爲不易之道下至蠻夷氏羌亦皆有
決疑之卜後世以是爲術數故俗儒有卜筮小
易之說蓋有見於今之卜筮也龜筮之法不傳
左氏所述多失之誣褚氏所録又失之鑿無怪
乎小易之說也雖然百筮之蓍十朋之龜不見
於世乂矣
===
書
庶土交正底慎財賦咸則三壤成賦中邦
華尚浩

考試官主事唐　批　〔場中作此者類多腐〕
punctuated:
之者哉？抑《易》爲卜筮作也，所以開物成務而利天下也。《周禮》建大卜、筮人之官，《書》建稽疑，而卜筮列五謀之二。古者國有大事，則必參之人謀，斷以蓍龜，爲不易之道。下至蠻夷氏羌，亦皆有決疑之卜。後世以是爲術數，故俗儒有卜筮小《易》之說，蓋有見於今之卜筮也。龜筮之法不傳，左氏所述多失之誣，褚氏所録又失之鑿，無怪乎小《易》之說也。雖然，百筮之蓍、十朋之龜，不見於世乂矣。

庶土交正，底慎財賦，咸則三壤，成賦中邦。
華尚浩

translation_en:
…what could surpass them? Moreover, the Book of Changes was composed for divination with turtle shells and milfoil, to disclose things, bring undertakings to completion, and benefit all under Heaven. The Rites of Zhou established the offices of Grand Diviner and Milfoil Diviner. The Book of Documents established the procedure for examining doubts, with turtle-shell and milfoil divination accounting for two of the five kinds of counsel. In antiquity, whenever the state faced a major undertaking, it invariably consulted human counsel and reached a decision through milfoil and turtle shells. This was regarded as an unchanging principle. Even the Man, Yi, Di [?], and Qiang all practiced divination to resolve doubts. Later generations regarded these practices as occult techniques. Hence commonplace scholars claimed that divination diminished the Book of Changes, presumably judging by the divination practiced in their own day. The methods of turtle-shell and milfoil divination have not been transmitted. Zuo’s accounts often err through fabrication, while Chu’s records err through strained interpretation. It is no wonder that people speak of diminishing the Book of Changes. Nevertheless, the milfoil used for a hundred divinations and the turtle worth ten pairs of shells have long [?] ceased to be seen in the world.

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
語是篇化腐爲新且底愼處能點出聖人心事
錄之
可見
考試官署郎中盧　批　當時經國之制宛然
史臣紀聖人之經國有因土以定貢者有因田
以定賦者蓋貢出于土而賦出于田也聖人因
之以定貢賦而無不致其謹焉其經國之制何
如哉想昔大禹當治水成功之後六府孔脩之
日以天下之大利既興而天下之財賦可出乃
===
于是而定其制焉是故九州庶土其等不同而
地利之美惡因之也定貢而不致其謹可乎禹
則于庶土而交相正之較其肥者瘠者與其高
下者焉于是物必指其所出之地地必表其所
產之良因地以制貢不責有于所無量出以爲
經不取美于其惡常出者定之以爲常偶得者
重之以爲異惟正之供圖備物以利用而厲民
自養猶兢兢焉恐失之濫也由中及外皆使土
而當其而損下益上猶惴惴焉懼取之盈也其
punctuated:
語。是篇化腐爲新，且底愼處能點出聖人心事，錄之，可見。
考試官署郎中盧批：當時經國之制宛然。
史臣紀聖人之經國，有因土以定貢者，有因田以定賦者。蓋貢出于土，而賦出于田也。聖人因之以定貢賦，而無不致其謹焉。其經國之制何如哉？想昔大禹，當治水成功之後、六府孔脩之日，以天下之大利既興，而天下之財賦可出，乃于是而定其制焉。是故九州庶土，其等不同，而地利之美惡因之也。定貢而不致其謹，可乎？禹則于庶土而交相正之，較其肥者、瘠者與其高下者焉。于是物必指其所出之地，地必表其所產之良。因地以制貢，不責有于所無；量出以爲經，不取美于其惡。常出者定之以爲常，偶得者重之以爲異。惟正之供，圖備物以利用，而厲民自養，猶兢兢焉恐失之濫也；由中及外，皆使土而當其，而損下益上，猶惴惴焉懼取之盈也。其
translation_en:
…language. This essay transforms the stale into the fresh; moreover, in treating “exercising care,” it brings out the sage’s inner concerns. Recorded here, these may be seen.
Examiner Lu, Acting Director, comments: The institutions for ordering the realm in that age are vividly presented.
When the court historian recorded the sage’s ordering of the realm, there were measures that determined tribute according to the soil and others that determined taxes according to the fields. For tribute derives from the soil, whereas taxes derive from cultivated fields. The sage used these as the basis for determining tribute and taxes, exercising the utmost care in every respect. What, then, were his institutions for ordering the realm? Consider Great Yu of old: after he had successfully brought the waters under control, when the Six Resources were thoroughly put in order, the great sources of benefit throughout the realm had been developed, and its revenues and taxes could be collected. He therefore established the institutions governing them.
Thus, the various soils of the Nine Provinces differed in grade, and the quality of the land’s yield varied accordingly. Could tribute be determined without the utmost care? Yu assessed the various soils against one another, comparing their fertility and barrenness, as well as their elevation. Every product was therefore assigned its place of origin, and each locality had its finest produce identified. Tribute was prescribed according to the land: nothing was demanded where it did not exist. Regular quotas were set by measuring output: fine produce was not extracted from inferior land. What was regularly produced was fixed as a regular contribution; what was only occasionally obtained was prized as exceptional. In providing only the proper contributions, he sought to assemble the full range of goods for useful purposes; yet he remained apprehensive lest he go too far and oppress the people to support himself. From the central regions to the outer territories, he ensured that each soil received its appropriate assignment [?]; yet he remained fearful lest he exact too much, diminishing those below to enrich those above. His…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
因土定貢者如此至若九州穀土其等不齊而
田賦之多寡各異也定賦而不則其壤可乎禹
故于穀土而第相則之品其上者中者與其下
下者焉于是總其綱而爲三列其目而爲九田
之上者上其賦隨次以定其等差田之下者賦
之下因田以分其輕重常者爲正歲之供錯者
爲間歲之出十一之規確乎不易而萬世所永
賴者信在是矣中邦之賦井乎有條而后世之
取民者此其則矣其因田定賦者如此是則曰
===
交正者土賦及于外夷曰則壤者田賦止于中
國聖人取民之義愛民之仁于是乎兩得之矣
抑禹貢之書有貢有賦貢惟服食器用而已賦
則有錯有三錯焉其規制周悉仁愛曲寓矣然
龍子曰治地莫不善于貢者豈其后世取民非
盡禹之制歟夫較數歲以爲常則洪水方降民
賦不以爲多而人工大脩之后乃以取盈爲病
何也且周室貢賦兼用者也周禮大司徒掌土
會土宜土均之灋以辨五物九等之異而制地
punctuated:
因土定貢者如此。至若九州穀土，其等不齊，而田賦之多寡各異也。定賦而不則其壤，可乎？禹故于穀土而第相則之，品其上者、中者與其下下者焉。于是總其綱而爲三，列其目而爲九。田之上者，上其賦，隨次以定其等差；田之下者，賦之下，因田以分其輕重。常者爲正歲之供，錯者爲間歲之出。十一之規，確乎不易，而萬世所永賴者，信在是矣。中邦之賦，井乎有條，而后世之取民者，此其則矣。其因田定賦者如此。是則曰「交正」者，土賦及于外夷；曰「則壤」者，田賦止于中國。聖人取民之義、愛民之仁，于是乎兩得之矣。
抑《禹貢》之書，有貢有賦。貢惟服食器用而已，賦則有錯、有三錯焉。其規制周悉，仁愛曲寓矣。然龍子曰：「治地莫不善于貢者。」豈其后世取民非盡禹之制歟？夫較數歲以爲常，則洪水方降，民賦不以爲多，而人工大脩之后，乃以取盈爲病，何也？且周室貢賦兼用者也。《周禮》大司徒掌土會、土宜、土均之灋，以辨五物九等之異，而制地
translation_en:
…Such was his determination of tribute according to the soil. As for the grain-producing soils of the Nine Provinces, their grades were unequal, and the amounts of land tax differed accordingly. Could taxes be fixed without taking the soil as their standard? Yu therefore graded the grain-producing soils against one another, ranking the superior, the middling, and the very poorest. He grouped them under three broad divisions and enumerated nine detailed grades. For superior fields he set a higher tax, determining its gradations in descending order; for inferior fields he set a lower tax, distinguishing heavier and lighter burdens according to the fields. Regular assessments supplied the annual levy; alternating assessments were delivered in alternate years. The rule of taking one tenth was firmly established and unchanging: here indeed lay what countless generations could rely upon forever. The taxes of the central realm were systematically ordered, providing a standard for later generations in collecting from the people. Such was his determination of taxes according to the fields. Thus, what is called “mutually adjusting” meant that levies on the produce of the soil extended to the outer non-Chinese peoples; what is called “taking the soil as the standard” meant that land taxes were confined to the central states. In this way, the sage achieved both righteousness in taking from the people and benevolence in caring for them.
Furthermore, the Tribute of Yu distinguishes tribute from taxation. Tribute consisted only of articles for clothing, food, and practical use, whereas taxation included alternating assessments and assessments alternating among three grades. Its institutions were comprehensive and detailed, with benevolent concern embodied in every particular. Yet Longzi said: “For governing the land, no system is worse than tribute.” Could it be that later generations, in taking from the people, did not fully follow Yu’s institutions? If the regular assessment was established by comparing several years’ yields, then, when the floodwaters had only just subsided, the people’s taxes were not considered excessive. Yet after human efforts had greatly improved the land, exacting the full assessment came to be regarded as a scourge. Why was this? Moreover, the Zhou dynasty used tribute and taxation together. According to the Rituals of Zhou, the Minister of Education administered the methods of land classification, determining the suitability of soils, and equalizing land assessments, distinguishing the five categories of products and the nine grades, and establishing land…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
征是固禹貢之遺也豈不善于夏而又用于周
乎悳故以爲成后世之過也
惟辟作福惟辟作威惟辟玉食
萬敏
