When the poet recounts King Wen’s quiet restraint, he necessarily prefaces it with: “Do not thus turn aside and stray; do not thus covet and desire.” Thus the achievements of his campaigns were assuredly brought about by sagely wisdom. When the Book of Documents recounts Cheng Tang’s campaign against Ge, it necessarily follows with: “The people’s support for Shang was indeed of long standing!” Thus the undertaking that inaugurated his rise to kingship was assuredly brought about by generosity and benevolence. Understanding this, we can speak of the victory at Pengli.
Alas, once the fortunes of the non-Han dynasty had declined, the people had no lord. The sagely ancestor received Heaven’s mandate and arose. With a single brigade he crossed the Yangzi; his newly founded enterprise was not yet consolidated. At that time there were such men as…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
僞漢陳氏僞吳張氏者兵甲之强財力之
富天下莫加焉友諒初自皖城而寇江州
又自江州而寇武昌屢肆侵軼輒厪師旅
方竊大號益據上游及是長圍豫章逆戰
彭蠡守者不能支謀者無虛日不得已躬
率將士以討之大戰五晝夜之間卒斃元
兇尋收遺孽先聲所訖逆節悉觧江漢之
水載清而鄱鄢之鼎斯固殆與湯文之舉
曠百世而同符者區區高光之功有不屑
===
論矣當是之時嘗折簡致龍灣之師出奇
以挫其鋒傳檄下龍興之郡用謀以斷其
臂聽劉基而感其取威定覇之言吐哺納
說之明也告戎簡而申以覆巢完卵之喻
因壘伐崇之意也
神謨廣略出自
聖衷誠有非臣下所得而預者然一代之興亦
豈無佐命者出於其間哉若徐武寧之身
先諸將摧破敵衝常忠武之矢殪賊徒奮
punctuated: 僞漢陳氏、僞吳張氏者，兵甲之强，財力之富，天下莫加焉。友諒初自皖城而寇江州，又自江州而寇武昌，屢肆侵軼，輒厪師旅。方竊大號，益據上游；及是長圍豫章，逆戰彭蠡，守者不能支，謀者無虛日。不得已，躬率將士以討之，大戰五晝夜之間，卒斃元兇，尋收遺孽。先聲所訖，逆節悉觧，江漢之水載清，而鄱鄢之鼎斯固。殆與湯文之舉，曠百世而同符者，區區高光之功，有不屑論矣。當是之時，嘗折簡致龍灣之師，出奇以挫其鋒；傳檄下龍興之郡，用謀以斷其臂。聽劉基而感其取威定覇之言，吐哺納說之明也；告戎簡而申以覆巢完卵之喻，因壘伐崇之意也。神謨廣略，出自聖衷，誠有非臣下所得而預者。然一代之興，亦豈無佐命者出於其間哉？若徐武寧之身先諸將，摧破敵衝；常忠武之矢殪賊徒，奮
translation_en:
…the Chen clan of the illegitimate Han regime and the Zhang clan of the illegitimate Wu regime, whose military strength and wealth were unsurpassed under Heaven. Youliang first advanced from Wancheng to raid Jiangzhou, then from Jiangzhou to raid Wuchang. His repeated incursions continually necessitated military action. Having usurped the imperial title, he further entrenched himself upstream. Now he subjected Yuzhang to a prolonged siege and offered resistance at Pengli. The defenders could not hold out, and those devising plans had not a day to spare. With no alternative, the emperor personally led his officers and soldiers to punish him. After a great battle lasting five days and nights, he finally slew the chief malefactor and soon subdued the remaining rebels. Wherever the advance report of his might reached, resistance dissolved. The waters of the Jiang and Han ran clear once more, and the dynastic tripod of Poyan [?] was thereby secured. These deeds accorded with those of Tang and King Wen across a gulf of a hundred generations; the paltry achievements of Gaozu and Guangwu scarcely merited discussion.

At that time, he once sent a brief letter to summon the forces at Longwan, employing surprise to blunt the enemy’s advance. He circulated a proclamation to bring Longxing Commandery into submission, using strategy to sever the enemy’s arm. He listened to Liu Ji and was moved by his words about establishing authority and securing supremacy: this showed the discernment of one who would spit out his food to receive counsel. He admonished Rong Jian [?], explaining further through the analogy of intact eggs beneath an overturned nest: this expressed the intent of attacking Chong by making use of existing siege works. His divine plans and far-reaching strategies issued from his sagely heart; truly, there were matters in which his servants could have no part. Yet when a dynasty rises, can there fail to appear men who assist in fulfilling its mandate? Consider Xu Wuning, who advanced ahead of all the other generals and smashed the enemy’s assault, or Chang Zhongwu, who felled the rebels with his arrows and exerted…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
力鏖戰以至俞通海廖永忠之輩孰非宣
力效忠者乎若韓成慕紀信之爲于明致
解揚之義業琛之死於洪都劉齊之死於
吉安以至趙得勝丁普郎之輩孰非伏節
死義者乎君臣之分未明而豪傑悉致死
力是固天惟純佑而生賢輔運者矣至其
吊伐之心遲速之會不有可言者乎夫遠
交近攻策士之謀舍近務遠兵家所忌孰
事以不先攻士誠而先及友諒爲疑愚聞
===
聖祖有言曰友諒剽而輕其志驕士誠狡而懦
其器小志驕則好生事器小則無遠圖若
先攻士誠友諒必空國而來是我疲於應
敵事有難爲先攻友諒士誠必不能踰姑
蘇一步以爲之援朕所以取二寇者固自
有先後也大哉
王言其智之盡乎所謂致人而不致于人者如
此觀其先取山東次及河洛次及幽薊次
及閩廣隴蜀以爲元都見之矣以居爲威
punctuated: 力鏖戰，以至俞通海、廖永忠之輩，孰非宣力效忠者乎？若韓成慕紀信之爲，于明致解揚之義，業琛之死於洪都，劉齊之死於吉安，以至趙得勝、丁普郎之輩，孰非伏節死義者乎？君臣之分未明，而豪傑悉致死力，是固天惟純佑而生賢輔運者矣。至其吊伐之心、遲速之會，不有可言者乎？夫遠交近攻，策士之謀；舍近務遠，兵家所忌。孰事以不先攻士誠而先及友諒爲疑？愚聞聖祖有言曰：「友諒剽而輕，其志驕；士誠狡而懦，其器小。志驕則好生事，器小則無遠圖。若先攻士誠，友諒必空國而來，是我疲於應敵，事有難爲。先攻友諒，士誠必不能踰姑蘇一步以爲之援。朕所以取二寇者，固自有先後也。」大哉，王言！其智之盡乎！所謂致人而不致于人者如此。觀其先取山東，次及河洛，次及幽薊，次及閩廣隴蜀，以爲元都見之矣，以居爲威
translation_en:
…fighting fiercely with all his strength; and men such as Yu Tonghai and Liao Yongzhong—who among them did not exert himself in loyal service? Han Cheng emulated Ji Xin’s deed; Yu Ming fulfilled the righteousness exemplified by Jie Yang; Ye Chen [?] died at Hongdu, and Liu Qi at Ji’an. Together with men such as Zhao Desheng and Ding Pulang, who among them did not uphold his integrity and die for righteousness? Even before the respective stations of ruler and subject had been clearly established, these outstanding men all exerted themselves to the death. Surely Heaven bestowed its fullest aid, bringing forth worthy men to assist the dynasty’s rise.

As for his intention to comfort the afflicted and punish the guilty, and his grasp of when to delay and when to act swiftly, is there not something to be said? Making distant alliances while attacking nearby enemies is the scheme of strategists; neglecting nearby objectives to pursue distant ones is what military experts avoid. Why, then, question his attacking Youliang before Shicheng [?]? I have heard that the sagely founder said: “Youliang is fierce and rash, and his ambitions are arrogant; Shicheng is cunning but timid, and his capacity is limited. Arrogant ambition makes a man eager to provoke trouble; limited capacity leaves him without far-reaching plans. If I attack Shicheng first, Youliang will certainly come with all the forces of his realm. I would then exhaust myself responding to the enemy, and matters would become difficult. If I attack Youliang first, Shicheng will certainly be unable to advance even one step beyond Gusu to assist him. In overcoming these two rebels, I have, of course, my own order of precedence.”

Great indeed are these royal words! How consummate their wisdom! This is what is meant by making others come to you rather than being made to go to them. Consider how he first took Shandong, then the He–Luo region, then You–Ji, and then Min, Guang, Long, and Shu. With regard to the Yuan capital, this could be seen [?]; by his position he established an intimidating presence [?]…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
舞方作慝縱暴以寬民其允懷執事又以
古之所以得天下者未必盡出於征伐爲
問題聞
聖祖有言曰群雄所爲强者縱暴貪者耽貨荒
淫者迷於子女剽賊者喜於戰鬪皆無救
患之心徒爲生民之患朕惟不嗜殺布信
義守勤儉故來者如歸大哉
王言其仁之至乎所謂得天下以仁者如此觀
其取金陵而市不易肆定浙東而兵不血
===
刃諭敵國以毋違天虐民戒將臣以毋虜
掠殺戮見之矣智之備故兵之所向者無
不克仁之盡故民之所從者不忍去此我
聖祖所以能一天下之速而非群雄之所能及
也雖然彭蠡之捷固足以定
國家萬世之大業矣愚則以爲守萬世之大
業者則又在燕薊之經營也蓋友諒未滅
天下之患猶在東南大業已定天下之患
恒在西北自古以來都金陵而混一天下
punctuated:
舞方作慝，縱暴以寬民，其允懷。執事又以古之所以得天下者未必盡出於征伐爲問。題聞聖祖有言曰：「群雄所爲，强者縱暴，貪者耽貨，荒淫者迷於子女，剽賊者喜於戰鬪，皆無救患之心，徒爲生民之患。朕惟不嗜殺，布信義，守勤儉，故來者如歸。」大哉，王言！其仁之至乎！所謂得天下以仁者如此。觀其取金陵而市不易肆，定浙東而兵不血刃，諭敵國以毋違天虐民，戒將臣以毋虜掠殺戮，見之矣。智之備，故兵之所向者無不克；仁之盡，故民之所從者不忍去。此我聖祖所以能一天下之速，而非群雄之所能及也。

雖然，彭蠡之捷固足以定國家萬世之大業矣。愚則以爲守萬世之大業者，則又在燕薊之經營也。蓋友諒未滅，天下之患猶在東南；大業已定，天下之患恒在西北。自古以來，都金陵而混一天下
translation_en:
…“Wu was then doing evil; indulging violence to bring relief to the people, they truly cherished him” [?]. You, gentlemen, further ask how those of antiquity who gained All under Heaven did not necessarily do so entirely through conquest. The question states [?] that our Sagely Founder once said: “Among the contending warlords, the strong indulged in violence, the greedy coveted wealth, the dissolute were infatuated with women, and the marauders delighted in warfare. None had any intention of relieving suffering; they merely brought suffering upon the people. I alone took no pleasure in killing, extended trustworthiness and righteousness, and upheld diligence and frugality. Thus those who came to me felt as though they were coming home.” How great are these royal words! Is this not benevolence in its utmost perfection? This is what is meant by gaining All under Heaven through benevolence. We can see it in his capture of Jinling, when the markets continued undisturbed; his pacification of eastern Zhejiang, when his soldiers did not bloody their blades; his admonitions to enemy states against defying Heaven and oppressing the people; and his injunctions to his generals against taking captives, plundering, and slaughtering. Because his wisdom was complete, wherever his armies advanced, they invariably prevailed. Because his benevolence was perfect, the people who followed him could not bear to leave. This is why our Sagely Founder was able to unite All under Heaven so swiftly, achieving what none of the contending warlords could match.

Nevertheless, although the victory at Pengli was indeed sufficient to establish the dynasty’s great enterprise for all generations, in my humble view the preservation of that enterprise for all generations depended also upon the strategic development of Yan and Ji. Before Youliang had been destroyed, the danger to All under Heaven still lay in the southeast; once the great enterprise had been secured, that danger lay continually in the northwest. From antiquity onward, those who established their capital at Jinling and united All under Heaven…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
者惟我
聖祖一人我
太宗文皇帝有見於此遂倣周室鎬京洛邑之
規審居重馭輕之計乃以燕薊爲行在居
之而以金陵爲留守之地百六十年來士
馬倚於西北財賦倚於東南食足兵强天
下至今賴之創造之艱繼述之美其功有
不當以軒輊者此執事之所未及愚故得
而併論之抑愚江西人也歲時有事康山
===
祠下獲拜死事諸臣凛凛乎猶有生氣未
始不肅然敬戚然哀也昔人觀河洛而思
禹執事方涉九江下彭蠡獨無感於
聖祖之功乎愚不敏倘獲與計吏偕尚當續宋
太史平江漢頌以爲
明廷獻
第二問
萬鈒
同考試官教諭曾　批〔寛嚴一策治體攸關〕
punctuated:
者，惟我聖祖一人。我太宗文皇帝有見於此，遂倣周室鎬京、洛邑之規，審居重馭輕之計，乃以燕薊爲行在，居之，而以金陵爲留守之地。百六十年來，士馬倚於西北，財賦倚於東南，食足兵强，天下至今賴之。創造之艱，繼述之美，其功有不當以軒輊者。此執事之所未及，愚故得而併論之。抑愚江西人也，歲時有事康山祠下，獲拜死事諸臣，凛凛乎猶有生氣，未始不肅然敬、戚然哀也。昔人觀河洛而思禹，執事方涉九江，下彭蠡，獨無感於聖祖之功乎？愚不敏，倘獲與計吏偕，尚當續宋太史《平江漢頌》，以爲明廷獻。

第二問
萬鈒
同考試官教諭曾　批〔寛嚴一策，治體攸關〕
translation_en:
…was our Sagely Founder alone. Our Emperor Wen, Taizong, perceived this and accordingly followed the Zhou royal house’s arrangement of Haojing and Luoyi. Having carefully considered the strategy of occupying the principal seat to control subordinate regions, he made Yan-Ji his temporary imperial residence and lived there, while leaving Jinling in the charge of officials who remained behind. For 160 years, troops and horses have depended on the northwest, while revenue has depended on the southeast. With food plentiful and the army strong, the realm has benefited from this to the present day. The arduous work of founding and the excellence of carrying forward that inheritance are achievements that ought not to be ranked one above the other. This is something you, sir, have not addressed, and so I have ventured to discuss both together.

Moreover, I am a native of Jiangxi. At the seasonal observances at the Kangshan shrine, I have been able to bow before the ministers who died in service. Their awe-inspiring presence seems still alive, and I have never failed to feel solemn reverence and poignant sorrow. People of old gazed upon the He and Luo rivers and thought of Yu. As you, sir, now cross Jiujiang and descend to Pengli, can you alone remain unmoved by the achievements of the Sagely Founder? Though I am untalented, if I should be permitted to accompany the tribute envoys, I would compose a continuation of Grand Historian Song’s Ode on Pacifying the Jiang and Han, to present to the Ming court.

Second Policy Question
Wan Sa 萬鈒
Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor, comments: 〔This policy essay on leniency and severity concerns the fundamental principles of governance.〕 …

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
古帝王馭天下率不越此是篇議擬有倫忠愛可即
其善于告君者
同考試官教諭何　批　酌古準今以仁字爲嘉
亦通達國體者録之
考試官王事居　批　是識治體者
考試官署郎中盧　批　得董賈筆意
蓋聞帝王之道天道也是故有寒暑陰陽
之時焉有剛柔刑賞之用焉凡以和育民
物順其長養而巳王者博愛無私執中和
===
之極以綏臨四方故當其時百官時叙萬
民雍和書曰同寅協恭和衷哉此堯舜之
世致治之極也今自書而觀之其稱堯曰
允恭克讓而巳其稱舜曰臨下以簡御衆
以寛而巳夫恭讓寛簡此聖人無爲之象
也聖人夫何爲哉如天之仁堯所以和萬
邦也好生之德舜所以協民心也而執事
乃以誅四凶討三苗爲舜病竊以爲過矣
夫堯舜之世其民同而其相繼也其道同
punctuated:
古帝王馭天下，率不越此。是篇議擬有倫，忠愛可即，其善于告君者。
同考試官教諭何批：酌古準今，以仁字爲嘉，亦通達國體者，録之。
考試官王事居批：是識治體者。
考試官署郎中盧批：得董賈筆意。
蓋聞帝王之道，天道也。是故有寒暑陰陽之時焉，有剛柔刑賞之用焉，凡以和育民物，順其長養而巳。王者博愛無私，執中和之極，以綏臨四方。故當其時，百官時叙，萬民雍和。《書》曰：「同寅協恭和衷哉！」此堯舜之世致治之極也。今自《書》而觀之，其稱堯曰：「允恭克讓」而巳；其稱舜曰：「臨下以簡，御衆以寛」而巳。夫恭讓寛簡，此聖人無爲之象也。聖人夫何爲哉？如天之仁，堯所以和萬邦也；好生之德，舜所以協民心也。而執事乃以誅四凶、討三苗爲舜病，竊以爲過矣。夫堯舜之世，其民同，而其相繼也，其道同。
translation_en:
…The ancient emperors and kings, in governing the realm, generally did not go beyond this. This essay’s arguments and comparisons are well ordered, and its loyalty and devotion are readily apparent. Its author is skilled at offering counsel to the ruler.
Associate Examiner He, Instructor, comments: Weighing antiquity against the present, it takes benevolence as its guiding excellence. Its author also comprehends the principles of governing the state. Accept it.
Examiner Wang Shiju comments: This is someone who understands the essentials of government.
Examiner Lu, Acting Director, comments: It captures the literary spirit of Dong Zhongshu and Jia Yi.
I have heard that the Way of emperors and kings is the Way of Heaven. Thus there are the seasons of cold and heat, yin and yang, and there are the applications of firmness and gentleness, punishment and reward. All serve to nurture the people and other living things harmoniously, fostering their growth. The true king loves all impartially and holds fast to the highest standard of equilibrium and harmony, thereby bringing peace to and presiding over the four quarters. Thus, in such an age, the hundred officials are duly ordered, and the myriad people live in concord. The Book of Documents says: “Be united in reverence, joined in respect, and harmonious in heart!” This was the perfection of good government in the age of Yao and Shun. Now, judging from the Book of Documents, its praise of Yao amounts simply to “truly reverent and capable of yielding,” and its praise of Shun simply to “presiding over those below with simplicity and governing the multitude with generosity.” Reverence, yielding, generosity, and simplicity are manifestations of the sage’s governing through nonaction. What, then, does the sage do? Through benevolence like Heaven’s, Yao brought the myriad states into harmony; through the virtue of cherishing life, Shun united the people’s hearts. Yet you, honored examiner, regard the punishment of the Four Malefactors and the campaign against the Sanmiao as faults in Shun. I venture to consider this mistaken. In the ages of Yao and Shun, the people were the same, and as one succeeded the other, their Way was the same…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
又奚不相沿之有且執事獨不見夫雷霆
之用乎其未震也寂然耳及夫不善之氣
應焉而奮擊隨之矣聖人之怒猶是也方
其怒也固用其天討有罪之心而其釋也
亦無損于鑑空衡平之體罪在人而怒在
彼聖人曷故焉仁者聖人之本心而或出
於威者聖人之所不得已也是故禹有禹
刑之制湯有官刑之儆文王有速殺之義
固矣夫獨不聞夫下車之泣哀百姓之無
===
知代虐以寬致兆民之允殖而惠鮮懷保
又足以綏西土而柔萬邦也哉且聖人制
刑非遽以刑人也詔之天下使預知所避
而法網無自入焉耳然亦非不刑人也刑
其所不得不刑而生其所當生者衆耳蠹
去則木茂矣螟蝗去則嘉穀昌矣故保善
仁也去不善以安善亦仁也誅一人而人
之不善者化亦仁也天不以無用之物而
廢其長養聖人不以不善之人而廢其仁
punctuated: 又奚不相沿之有？且執事獨不見夫雷霆之用乎？其未震也，寂然耳；及夫不善之氣應焉，而奮擊隨之矣。聖人之怒猶是也。方其怒也，固用其天討有罪之心；而其釋也，亦無損于鑑空衡平之體。罪在人，而怒在彼，聖人曷故焉？仁者，聖人之本心；而或出於威者，聖人之所不得已也。是故禹有禹刑之制，湯有官刑之儆，文王有速殺之義，固矣。夫獨不聞夫下車之泣，哀百姓之無知；代虐以寬，致兆民之允殖；而惠鮮懷保，又足以綏西土而柔萬邦也哉？且聖人制刑，非遽以刑人也，詔之天下，使預知所避，而法網無自入焉耳。然亦非不刑人也，刑其所不得不刑，而生其所當生者衆耳。蠹去則木茂矣，螟蝗去則嘉穀昌矣。故保善，仁也；去不善以安善，亦仁也；誅一人而人之不善者化，亦仁也。天不以無用之物而廢其長養，聖人不以不善之人而廢其仁
translation_en:
…what failure to continue their predecessors’ ways could there have been? Moreover, have you not observed how thunder works? Before it sounds, all is still; when malign forces call forth a response, its mighty strike follows. The sage’s anger is just like this. When angry, he indeed acts upon his resolve to carry out Heaven’s punishment of the guilty; when his anger subsides, it has done no harm to his essential nature, clear as an empty mirror and impartial as a level balance. The guilt lies with the offender, and the anger is directed at him: what personal motive has the sage in this? Benevolence is the sage’s original heart; when he sometimes resorts to severity, he does so only because he has no alternative. Thus Yu established the Punishments of Yu, Tang issued the admonitions of the Punishments for Officials, and King Wen upheld the principle of prompt execution. This is certainly so. Yet have you not heard how Yu descended from his carriage and wept, grieving at the people’s ignorance; how Tang replaced tyranny with leniency, bringing true prosperity to the multitude; and how King Wen showed kindness to the helpless and cherished and protected the people, thereby pacifying the western lands and winning the allegiance of the myriad states?

Moreover, when sages establish punishments, they do not immediately use them to punish people. They proclaim them throughout the realm so that people may know beforehand what to avoid and thus keep themselves from entering the net of the law. Yet this does not mean that they punish no one. They punish those whom they cannot but punish, while those whose lives they rightly preserve are many. Remove the borers, and the trees flourish; remove the caterpillars and locusts, and the fine grain thrives. Thus protecting the good is benevolence; removing the wicked to secure the good is also benevolence; executing one person so that others who are wicked reform is likewise benevolence. Heaven does not abandon its nurturing of things because some are useless; the sage does not abandon his benevolence because some people are wicked …

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
愛夫固使其誅罰之心不勝其好生之德
而已耳是故其所生者衆而其不可化而
就誅者終帝王之世而無一二也夫斷獄
三百后世以爲有刑措之風數十年而一
二誅也而以爲聖人之尚威其不爲誣聖
人矣乎况夫道久化成仁漸義被卒之五
刑虛設而已耳嗟乎聖人之德尚矣聖人
之世遠矣于漢吾得文帝焉躬脩玄嘿以
德化民所謂不盡人之財不盡人之力不
===
盡人之情者是也卒之黎民殷庶興于禮
義而漢氏之業培養益深矣或者乃有孝
宣優于孝文之說夫宣帝之勵精固足爲
中興之主而其任刑名也適以敝漢氏之
業而已又豈可以與文帝同語乎于宋吾
得仁宗焉恭儉明恕始終如一所謂刑以
不殺爲威財以不蓄爲富兵以不用爲功
者是也卒之人心目固而社稷靈長終有
賴之矣或者亦有國勢不振之議夫豈若
punctuated: 愛，夫固使其誅罰之心不勝其好生之德而已耳。是故其所生者衆，而其不可化而就誅者，終帝王之世而無一二也。夫斷獄三百，后世以爲有刑措之風；數十年而一二誅也，而以爲聖人之尚威，其不爲誣聖人矣乎？况夫道久化成，仁漸義被，卒之五刑虛設而已耳。嗟乎！聖人之德尚矣，聖人之世遠矣！于漢吾得文帝焉，躬脩玄嘿，以德化民，所謂不盡人之財、不盡人之力、不盡人之情者是也。卒之黎民殷庶，興于禮義，而漢氏之業培養益深矣。或者乃有孝宣優于孝文之說。夫宣帝之勵精，固足爲中興之主，而其任刑名也，適以敝漢氏之業而已，又豈可以與文帝同語乎？于宋吾得仁宗焉，恭儉明恕，始終如一，所謂刑以不殺爲威、財以不蓄爲富、兵以不用爲功者是也。卒之人心目固，而社稷靈長，終有賴之矣。或者亦有國勢不振之議。夫豈若
translation_en:
…benevolent love. He simply ensures that his desire to punish and execute does not outweigh his virtue of cherishing life. Thus, those whose lives he preserves are many, while those who cannot be transformed and must be executed do not number even one or two throughout an emperor’s reign. When three hundred criminal cases were adjudicated, later generations considered this to have the character of an age when punishments were set aside. Yet when one or two people are executed over several decades, they take this as evidence that the sage prizes coercive authority. Is this not slandering the sage? Moreover, when the Way has long prevailed and moral transformation is complete, when benevolence has permeated and righteousness has spread, the Five Punishments ultimately remain established but unused.

Alas! How exalted is the virtue of the sages, and how distant their age! In the Han, I find Emperor Wen: he personally cultivated profound quietude and transformed the people through virtue. He exemplified the saying that one should not exhaust the people’s wealth, exhaust their strength, or make excessive demands upon their feelings. In the end, the common people prospered and multiplied, rites and righteousness flourished among them, and the foundations of the Han dynasty were nurtured ever more deeply. Some, however, claim that Emperor Xiaoxuan surpassed Emperor Xiaowen. Emperor Xuan’s vigorous efforts certainly qualified him as a ruler who restored the dynasty’s fortunes. Yet his reliance on punishments and the scrutiny of titles and performance served only to weaken the Han’s foundations. How could he be spoken of in the same terms as Emperor Wen?

In the Song, I find Emperor Renzong: respectful, frugal, discerning, and forbearing, he remained consistent from beginning to end. He exemplified the saying that punishments derive their authority from not killing, wealth its abundance from not being hoarded, and arms their achievement from not being used. In the end, the people’s allegiance became firm [?], and the dynasty endured, sustained throughout by his legacy. Some, however, also criticize the failure to strengthen the state’s power. But could this compare with…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
神宗用兵人盡改祖宗之法而用兵西
北卒敝天下之財者哉夫古之聖人非不
知嚴迫之足以立功而故爲是寬和之化
也誠以建國家者貴有沃澤深仁爲萬世
不拔之基而不貴目前可喜一敝不復之
政耳是故刑罰者聖人所不能廢而忠厚
者其本也德胥威而久立政藉法而后行
夫固有先后而已必之仁矣則雖誅數人
而不害其爲仁先有意于威則雖一言之
===
詰責一人之受誣而仁之體虧矣故治有
本原政有先務勢有所必行時有所不可
君人者在審其端使可繼之下而已朝廷
有寬和之實則太臣有休休之量矣故無
弗師師而尚德者焉百工播推讓之風萬
民興禮遜之行至和純龎而治道其幾矣
人主有督察之實則大臣多鷙厲之行矣
故無弗師師而尚威者焉群臣飭知以自
駭庶民懷私而喜爭和氣不流而剛暴之
punctuated: 神宗用兵，人盡改祖宗之法，而用兵西北，卒敝天下之財者哉？夫古之聖人非不知嚴迫之足以立功，而故爲是寬和之化也，誠以建國家者貴有沃澤深仁，爲萬世不拔之基，而不貴目前可喜、一敝不復之政耳。是故刑罰者，聖人所不能廢，而忠厚者其本也。德胥威而久立，政藉法而后行，夫固有先后而已。必之仁矣，則雖誅數人，而不害其爲仁；先有意于威，則雖一言之詰責、一人之受誣，而仁之體虧矣。故治有本原，政有先務，勢有所必行，時有所不可。君人者在審其端，使可繼之下而已。朝廷有寬和之實，則太臣有休休之量矣，故無弗師師而尚德者焉。百工播推讓之風，萬民興禮遜之行，至和純龎，而治道其幾矣。人主有督察之實，則大臣多鷙厲之行矣，故無弗師師而尚威者焉。群臣飭知以自駭，庶民懷私而喜爭，和氣不流，而剛暴之
translation_en:
…could he be compared with Shenzong, who resorted to warfare, completely changed the laws of his imperial ancestors [?], and campaigned in the northwest, ultimately exhausting the wealth of the realm? The sages of antiquity were not unaware that severity and coercion could achieve results; nevertheless, they deliberately pursued transformation through generosity and mildness. They truly understood that those who establish a state should prize abundant beneficence and profound benevolence as a foundation that would remain unshaken for ten thousand generations. They should not prize policies pleasing for the moment but incapable of recovery once they fail. Thus, punishments are something the sages cannot abolish, yet conscientious generosity is their foundation. Virtue depends upon authority to endure, and government relies upon law to operate: there is simply an order of precedence between them. If benevolence is made primary [?], then even executing several people does not compromise one's benevolence. But if one first sets one's mind on asserting authority, then even a single word of reproach or a single person's being falsely accused impairs the substance of benevolence. Thus, good rule has its foundations, and government its priorities; circumstances may require action, while the times may render it inadmissible. The ruler's task is simply to examine the initiating principle carefully, so that those below may carry it forward.

When generosity and mildness genuinely prevail at court, the great ministers possess a capacious tolerance; all follow one another in honoring virtue. The officials spread a spirit of deference, and the people cultivate conduct marked by ritual propriety and modest yielding. Perfect harmony becomes pure and abundant, and the Way of good government is nearly attained. When the ruler actively scrutinizes and supervises, the great ministers often behave fiercely and harshly; all follow one another in honoring coercive authority. The assembled ministers marshal their cleverness in fearful self-protection [?], while the common people harbor private interests and delight in contention. Harmonious influences cease to circulate, and harsh and violent…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
政漸成矣此王伯之異盛衰之會也可不
愼與雖然二者之間有機焉亦善其用而
已矣當庶政隳廢之后而不以勵精起之
則日靡月玩國柄漸移此致危之道也及
夫隳者舉矣廢者興矣而不以寬和養之
則旬磨歲鍛元氣日瀉此致亂之術也書
曰明作有功惇大成裕此之謂也方今
聖天子當積敝之后建精明之功行且致平康
之盛收無爲之化而斥剛柔于不用矣執
===
事猶以仁威之異下詢諸生此固憂治世
危
明主之盛心而愚生一得之見亦弗敢隱也故
敬以告之執事不識可轉聞于
上否
第三問
劉伯躍
同考試官教諭羅　批〔課證一策正觀諸子惇甫〕
〔今之學場中多爲所窘者遽悉而議論是然逾此篇〕
punctuated:
政漸成矣。此王伯之異、盛衰之會也，可不愼與？雖然，二者之間有機焉，亦善其用而已矣。當庶政隳廢之后，而不以勵精起之，則日靡月玩，國柄漸移，此致危之道也。及夫隳者舉矣，廢者興矣，而不以寬和養之，則旬磨歲鍛，元氣日瀉，此致亂之術也。《書》曰：「明作有功，惇大成裕。」此之謂也。方今聖天子當積敝之后，建精明之功，行且致平康之盛，收無爲之化，而斥剛柔于不用矣。執事猶以仁威之異下詢諸生，此固憂治世、危明主之盛心，而愚生一得之見亦弗敢隱也，故敬以告之。執事不識可轉聞于上否？

第三問
劉伯躍
同考試官教諭羅　批〔課證一策，正觀諸子惇甫〕〔今之學場中多爲所窘者，遽悉而議論是然逾此篇〕
translation_en:
…harsh and violent government gradually takes shape. Here lies the distinction between kingly and hegemonic rule, and the juncture between flourishing and decline. Can one fail to be cautious? Nevertheless, there is a critical opportunity in the interplay of these two approaches: everything depends on using them well. When the various affairs of government have fallen into neglect, failure to revive them through diligent effort leads to daily deterioration and prolonged complacency, while control of the state gradually passes into other hands. This is the road to peril. Once neglected affairs have been taken up and abandoned undertakings revived, however, failure to nurture them with leniency and harmony subjects them to grinding and hammering, ten-day period after ten-day period, year after year, draining their vital energy daily. This is a method for bringing about disorder. The Book of Documents says: “Act with discernment, and there will be achievement; through generosity and breadth, bring abundance to completion.” This is what it means.

Now our sagely Son of Heaven, coming after a period of accumulated abuses, has achieved results through discernment and diligence. Soon he will bring about flourishing peace and well-being, attain the transforming influence of government through nonaction, and set aside both harshness and leniency as unnecessary. Yet you, sir, still condescend to question us students about the distinction between benevolence and authority. This surely expresses your profound concern for dangers even in a well-governed age under an enlightened ruler. Nor dare I, an ignorant student, conceal the one insight I have gained; thus I respectfully present it to you. Might you, sir, convey it to His Majesty?

Third Policy Question
Liu Boyue
Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: 〔This policy essay on assessment and verification … rightly examines the various masters … Dunfu [?].〕〔In present-day examination writing, many are stymied by this … comprehensive … its argument … surpasses this essay [?].〕

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官 教諭沈 批〔典實明快取之〕
考試官主事屠 批〔補偏救敝之策〕
考試官署郎中盧 批〔可舉而措之者〕
公天下之黜陟定百世之榮辱者有先王
考課謚法存焉二者皆人君之所以馭其
臣先王之法不可一日而廢也夫立法者
具其文而行法者稽其實不稽其實而惟
其文之徇則毀譽亂眞予奪失當徒法而
已耳其何以彰善惡而示勸懲哉請以是
===
復執事之問昔者虞廷肇建官職班制四
嶽乃立課以考功後世從而推廣之三歲
而計其治九載而會其成功罪既明而黜
陟加焉其法自周官而後若西漢之六條
檢察東京之三公奏課又有京房劉邵杜
恕崔鴻諸人之議純疵不一惟杜預所建
則有實跡而無矯飾殆後世所當遵者乎
周家開嗣王業建功牧野乃制謚以易名
後世從而擬議之大行受大名細行受細
punctuated:
同考試官教諭沈批〔典實明快，取之。〕
考試官主事屠批〔補偏救敝之策。〕
考試官署郎中盧批〔可舉而措之者。〕

公天下之黜陟，定百世之榮辱者，有先王考課謚法存焉。二者皆人君之所以馭其臣，先王之法不可一日而廢也。夫立法者具其文，而行法者稽其實。不稽其實，而惟其文之徇，則毀譽亂眞，予奪失當，徒法而已耳。其何以彰善惡而示勸懲哉？請以是復執事之問。

昔者虞廷肇建官職，班制四嶽，乃立課以考功。後世從而推廣之，三歲而計其治，九載而會其成，功罪既明而黜陟加焉。其法自周官而後，若西漢之六條檢察，東京之三公奏課，又有京房、劉邵、杜恕、崔鴻諸人之議，純疵不一。惟杜預所建，則有實跡而無矯飾，殆後世所當遵者乎？

周家開嗣王業，建功牧野，乃制謚以易名。後世從而擬議之，大行受大名，細行受細
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor, comments: 〔Substantial and well grounded, clear and brisk. Accept it.〕
Examiner Tu, Secretary, comments: 〔A policy essay that corrects imbalances and remedies abuses.〕
Examiner Lu, Acting Director, comments: 〔These proposals can be put into practice.〕

To make demotions and promotions impartial throughout the realm, and to determine honor and disgrace for a hundred generations, there survive the former kings’ systems of performance evaluation and posthumous naming. Both are means by which a ruler governs his ministers; the former kings’ laws must not be abandoned for even a day. Those who establish laws supply their written provisions, while those who administer them examine the actual facts. If they do not examine the facts but merely follow the written provisions, disparagement and praise will obscure the truth, and rewards and deprivations will be inappropriate. There will be nothing but laws on paper. How could these make goodness and wickedness manifest and provide encouragement and deterrence? Allow me to answer your question on this basis.

In ancient times, the court of Yu first established official posts and apportioned responsibilities to the Four Chiefs; it then instituted evaluations to assess merit. Later generations extended this system: every three years they assessed officials’ administration, and every nine years they reviewed their accomplishments together. Once merits and faults were clear, demotions and promotions followed. After the Offices of Zhou, such systems included the Western Han’s inspections under the Six Articles and the Eastern Han’s performance reports submitted by the Three Dukes. There were also proposals by Jing Fang, Liu Shao, Du Shu, Cui Hong, and others, varying in their soundness and defects. Only the system proposed by Du Yu rested on actual achievements without false embellishment. Was this perhaps what later generations ought to have followed?

The house of Zhou inaugurated and carried forward its royal enterprise [?] and established its achievement at Muye. It then instituted posthumous titles to replace personal names. Later generations followed this precedent in deliberating upon such titles: great conduct received a great name, and lesser conduct received a lesser…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
名美惡一定而榮辱係焉其法自周公帝
下有春秋魔謚尚書世本又有蔡邕賀琛
沈約扈蒙諸家之書踳駁爲甚惟蘇洵所
編則去取精而輕重別殆前人所未及者
乎夫有其人以行其法法固未嘗不善也
然或有如王成桑縪者則反以無實而封
以有過而舉如段文昌則已署下考奏入
不報謂考課之皆得其實未也亦有如賈
充許敬宗者則反以奸逆謚武以貪媚謚
===
恭如夏竦則巳謚文正爭之乃改謂賜謚
之盡出於公未也若此者豈非不究其實
而徒狥其文之過哉斯固天下之通患也
夫百僚師師百工惟時古之時不待考課
而有所加勸也後世有課望之巳淺然猶
各注其任官之蹟以爲課詞而載采之意
存焉執事曰考課不先得其善最之狀則
藻鑑必迷蓋唐世課法以德義清慎恪勤
公平定爲四善以總之而於拾遺補過則
punctuated:
名，美惡一定，而榮辱係焉。其法自周公帝下，有《春秋魔謚》《尚書》《世本》，又有蔡邕、賀琛、沈約、扈蒙諸家之書，踳駁爲甚。惟蘇洵所編，則去取精而輕重別，殆前人所未及者乎！夫有其人以行其法，法固未嘗不善也。然或有如王成、桑縪者，則反以無實而封，以有過而舉；如段文昌，則已署下考，奏入不報，謂考課之皆得其實，未也。亦有如賈充、許敬宗者，則反以奸逆謚武，以貪媚謚恭；如夏竦，則巳謚文正，爭之乃改，謂賜謚之盡出於公，未也。若此者，豈非不究其實而徒狥其文之過哉？斯固天下之通患也。
夫百僚師師，百工惟時，古之時不待考課而有所加勸也。後世有課，望之巳淺，然猶各注其任官之蹟，以爲課詞，而載采之意存焉。執事曰：「考課不先得其善最之狀，則藻鑑必迷。」蓋唐世課法，以德義、清慎、恪勤、公平定爲四善以總之，而於拾遺補過則
translation_en:
…names. Once goodness and wickedness were definitively judged, honor and disgrace depended upon that judgment. From the Duke of Zhou onward [?], the rules were recorded in the Spring and Autumn Posthumous Names [?], the Book of Documents, and the Genealogical Records, as well as in works by Cai Yong, He Chen, Shen Yue, Hu Meng, and others. These were exceedingly inconsistent and contradictory. Only Su Xun’s compilation was discriminating in what it retained or rejected and distinguished the relative weight of judgments. Was this perhaps an achievement beyond his predecessors? With the right people to implement these rules, the rules themselves were certainly sound. Yet men such as Wang Cheng and Sang Bi [?] were, perversely, enfeoffed without actual accomplishments or recommended despite their faults. Duan Wenchang had already been assigned the lowest assessment, but the memorial reporting it received no response. Thus one cannot say that performance evaluations invariably reflected the facts. Likewise, men such as Jia Chong and Xu Jingzong were, perversely, given the posthumous names Wu, “Martial,” despite treachery and disloyalty, and Gong, “Respectful,” despite greed and flattery. Xia Song had already been given the posthumous name Wenzheng, “Cultured and Upright,” and it was changed only after objections were raised. Thus one cannot say that the granting of posthumous names was invariably impartial. Are such cases not the result of failing to investigate the substance and merely following outward forms? This is indeed a universal failing throughout the realm.
When “the hundred officials took one another as models, and all officers duly fulfilled their duties,” men in antiquity were encouraged to greater effort without waiting for performance evaluations. Later ages instituted evaluations, setting lower expectations for officials. Nevertheless, each official’s achievements in office were recorded to furnish the wording of his assessment, thereby preserving the intention of recording accomplishments. You, honored examiners, say: “Unless performance evaluations first ascertain the particulars of officials’ virtues and outstanding achievements, discerning judgment will inevitably go astray.” Under the Tang system of evaluation, moral integrity, purity and circumspection, conscientious diligence, and fairness were established as the Four Virtues that provided its general framework. As for supplying omissions and remedying errors, these were…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
爲近侍之最擢盡才能則爲選司之最以
類而分凡二十有七焉取善最之實而行
杜預之法庶乎其近古耳大上立德其次
立功古之人雖無贈謚而夫曾自怠也後
世有謚待之已薄然猶各哀其平生之行
以爲謚議而節惠之意存焉執事曰議謚
而不先去其傅會之詞則斷斷何在蓋舊
本謚法以巧言如流曰智闢于四門曰穆
取諸詩書而名之而牝晨家索取之易以
===
爲索並后匹適取之春秋以爲並以辭害
意殆難以盡述焉去傅會之詞而質之於
蘇洵之書庶乎其不謬耳
國家稽古爲治內外之考則叅三年六年之
制而並用之大臣之謚則采大行細行之
實而量賜之是也然勞效自叙者多任意
舉劾所及者或失衷而數十言之間無以
盡一人之情僞獻議不由於博士覆定不
關於考功而一二人之見無以定百世之
punctuated:
爲近侍之最，擢盡才能則爲選司之最，以類而分，凡二十有七焉。取善最之實而行杜預之法，庶乎其近古耳。大上立德，其次立功。古之人雖無贈謚，而夫曾自怠也。後世有謚，待之已薄，然猶各哀其平生之行，以爲謚議，而節惠之意存焉。執事曰：「議謚而不先去其傅會之詞，則斷斷何在？」蓋舊本謚法，以巧言如流曰智，闢于四門曰穆，取諸詩書而名之；而牝晨家索，取之易以爲索；並后匹適，取之春秋以爲並。以辭害意，殆難以盡述焉。去傅會之詞而質之於蘇洵之書，庶乎其不謬耳。
國家稽古爲治，內外之考，則叅三年六年之制而並用之；大臣之謚，則采大行細行之實而量賜之，是也。然勞效自叙者多任意，舉劾所及者或失衷，而數十言之間無以盡一人之情僞；獻議不由於博士，覆定不關於考功，而一二人之見無以定百世之
translation_en:
…constitutes the highest merit for close attendants; promoting men so that their talents are fully employed constitutes the highest merit for officials responsible for selection. Distinguished by category, there are twenty-seven such criteria in all. If the actual substance of these virtues and merits were ascertained and Du Yu’s method applied, this might approach ancient practice.
The highest achievement is to establish virtue; next comes establishing meritorious deeds. Although men of antiquity received no posthumous honors or names, they never grew negligent [?]. In later ages, posthumous names were instituted, reflecting an already diminished estimation of men. Nevertheless, each man’s lifelong conduct was still mournfully considered in preparing the deliberation on his posthumous name, preserving the intention of summarizing his conduct to bestow an honor. You say: “If strained interpretations are not first eliminated from deliberations on posthumous names, where is the firm judgment?” The old text of the Rules for Posthumous Names takes “clever speech flowing like a stream” as grounds for the name Zhi, “Wise,” and “opening the four gates” as grounds for Mu, “Reverent.” It draws these expressions from the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents to establish the names. Again, it takes “when the hen announces the dawn, the household is exhausted” from the Book of Changes to establish Suo, “Exhausted,” and “setting a consort alongside the queen and a rival alongside the legitimate heir” from the Spring and Autumn Annals to establish Bing, “Rival.” Instances of allowing wording to distort meaning can scarcely all be enumerated. If these strained interpretations were eliminated and the matter checked against Su Xun’s book, errors might perhaps be avoided.
Our dynasty consults antiquity in its governance. In evaluating officials within and outside the capital, it combines the systems of triennial and sexennial evaluation, employing both. In granting posthumous names to high ministers, it gathers the facts of their major and minor acts and bestows names as appropriate. This is right. Yet those who recount their own service and achievements often do so as they please; recommendations and impeachments sometimes miss the mark. A few dozen words cannot fully convey what is genuine or false in a man’s character. Proposals for posthumous names do not originate with the Erudites, nor does their review and confirmation involve the Bureau of Evaluations. The views of one or two men cannot determine, for a hundred generations, …

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
是非故有功者上無功者亦上厥是一出
或不免於道路之喧歷賢者與不賢者亦
與易名未下或有待其子孫之祈懇誠有
未足以厭公議以蓋平生如執事所云者
寔悖乎勸懲之效不如古昔哉然是二者
爲法則異爲訓則同勢相因而事相濟也
何也考課行於當仕之日贈謚行於既歿
之後考課不及於貴近贈謚不及於下僚
其生也或以倖免或以枉抑其歿也得以
===
追貶得以追雪蓋不惟儆于有位雖晚節
末路有不敢以肆焉者其法不亦重乎其
訓不亦嚴乎但古今異宜斟酌損益與時
偕行懲竊又有以告執事者今天下人才
日盛風俗日下功利重而廉耻輕諂諛盛
而忠信薄知其淪胥而不知其所底止此
賈生所以大息於漢文之朝夫亦見其微
也爲今之計必先正今之俗不必大變今
之法又必慎簡其人以責其法之必行法
punctuated:
是非。故有功者上，無功者亦上，厥是一出，或不免於道路之喧歷；賢者與，不賢者亦與，易名未下，或有待其子孫之祈懇。誠有未足以厭公議、以蓋平生，如執事所云者，寔悖乎勸懲之效，不如古昔哉！然是二者，爲法則異，爲訓則同，勢相因而事相濟也。何也？考課行於當仕之日，贈謚行於既歿之後；考課不及於貴近，贈謚不及於下僚。其生也，或以倖免，或以枉抑；其歿也，得以追貶，得以追雪。蓋不惟儆于有位，雖晚節末路，有不敢以肆焉者。其法不亦重乎？其訓不亦嚴乎？但古今異宜，斟酌損益，與時偕行。
懲竊又有以告執事者：今天下人才日盛，風俗日下，功利重而廉耻輕，諂諛盛而忠信薄，知其淪胥而不知其所底止。此賈生所以大息於漢文之朝，夫亦見其微也。爲今之計，必先正今之俗，不必大變今之法；又必慎簡其人，以責其法之必行。法
translation_en:
…right and wrong. Thus those with meritorious service are advanced, but those without it are also advanced. Once these assessments are issued [?], they sometimes provoke public outcry [?]. The worthy receive posthumous titles, but the unworthy receive them too; sometimes the decree conferring a posthumous name is withheld until their descendants plead earnestly for it. There are indeed cases, as you have said, in which these judgments fail to satisfy public opinion or adequately sum up a lifetime. This truly defeats their purpose of encouragement and punishment: how inferior to ancient practice!
Yet these two institutions, though different as regulations, convey the same admonition; their operation is interdependent, and their functions complement one another. Why is this? Performance evaluations take place during an official’s service, whereas posthumous titles are conferred after death. Performance evaluations do not extend to the highly placed and those close to the throne, while posthumous titles do not extend to subordinate officials. During life, some escape censure through good fortune, while others suffer unjust suppression; after death, they can be retrospectively degraded or exonerated. Thus these practices admonish not only those holding office: even toward the close of their careers and lives, men dare not behave without restraint. Are these regulations not weighty? Are their admonitions not stern? Nevertheless, what is fitting differs between ancient and modern times; additions and reductions must be weighed so that institutions advance with the times.
I venture to offer you a further observation [the preceding character 懲 is uncertain]. Today, talented men throughout the realm grow daily more numerous, yet customs deteriorate daily. Achievement and profit are valued, while integrity and shame are slighted; flattery flourishes, while loyalty and trustworthiness decline. We recognize the general descent but do not know where it will end. This is why Master Jia sighed so deeply at the court of Emperor Wen of Han: he too perceived the subtle beginnings of decline. The proper course today must first be to rectify present customs; there is no need for sweeping changes to present regulations. Moreover, men must be selected with care and held responsible for ensuring that those regulations are implemented. The regulations…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
立而能守則士習可變風俗可正三代之
治不難復也昔人論考課其本在於至公
至明而其責歸於天子宰相至哉言也何
獨謚法而不然然則欲循名責實而立法
以勸懲其大本宜不出此執事幸勿以為
僭也
第四問
鄧秀
同考試官教諭白　批〔是亦抱先憂後樂之志者〕
===
同考試官教諭張　批〔足國裕民之道區畫詳審不〕
〔迂不拘此必素養之士也〕
考試官主事屠　批〔用世之文〕
考試官署郎中盧　批〔深識時務〕
執事發策以歷代田賦為問而拳拳於
國家田賦之未能復古民生之未能無困誠
抱先天下之憂者也愚敢無辭而對夏商
以前其詳不可得聞矣周人始為井田在
鄉遂者遂人所掌其法用貢在都鄙者匠
punctuated:
立而能守，則士習可變，風俗可正，三代之治不難復也。昔人論考課，其本在於至公至明，而其責歸於天子宰相。至哉言也！何獨謚法而不然？然則欲循名責實，而立法以勸懲，其大本宜不出此。執事幸勿以為僭也。

第四問
鄧秀
同考試官教諭白　批〔是亦抱先憂後樂之志者。〕
同考試官教諭張　批〔足國裕民之道，區畫詳審，不〕〔迂不拘，此必素養之士也。〕
考試官主事屠　批〔用世之文。〕
考試官署郎中盧　批〔深識時務。〕

執事發策，以歷代田賦為問，而拳拳於國家田賦之未能復古、民生之未能無困，誠抱先天下之憂者也。愚敢無辭而對？夏商以前，其詳不可得聞矣。周人始為井田，在鄉遂者，遂人所掌，其法用貢；在都鄙者，匠
translation_en:
…once established and upheld, the habits of scholars can be transformed and social customs rectified; restoring the governance of the Three Dynasties would not be difficult. An earlier writer, discussing the evaluation of officials, held that its foundation lay in utmost impartiality and discernment, and that responsibility for it rested with the Son of Heaven and the chief councilors. How profound these words are! Why should the rules for conferring posthumous titles alone be otherwise? Thus, if one wishes to hold actual conduct accountable to names and establish rules to encourage and admonish, the fundamental principle should be no different. I hope you will not consider these remarks presumptuous.

Fourth Policy Question
Deng Xiu
Associate Examiner Bai, Instructor, comments: 〔This too is a man who cherishes the aspiration to worry before others and enjoy happiness after them.〕
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔His plans for making the state adequately supplied and the people prosperous are detailed and carefully considered, neither〕〔impractical nor rigid. He must be a scholar of longstanding cultivation.〕
Examiner Tu, Secretary, comments: 〔Writing suited to practical service in the world.〕
Examiner Lu, Acting Bureau Director, comments: 〔A deep understanding of contemporary affairs.〕

You have issued a policy question concerning land taxation through successive dynasties, expressing earnest concern that our state's land taxation has not yet been restored to ancient practice and that the people's livelihood has not yet been freed from hardship. Truly, you cherish the wish to worry before all others under Heaven. How could I, ignorant though I am, dare offer no words in reply? Details of the Xia and Shang and earlier times can no longer be ascertained. The people of Zhou first instituted the well-field system. Fields in the townships and outer districts were administered by the Director of Outlying Districts, and their method of taxation was tribute; those in the metropolitan and outlying domains were administered by the master artisan …

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
人所掌其法用助商鞅決裂阡陌田不井
授賦無定制於是先王之迹熄而兼并之
勢成漢高帝起而悉去秦法自今觀之秦
之虐政莫大於廢井田漢之更化亦莫大
於復井田也亂極甫治土曠寡民可復而
不復是果啓導之無人而經理之未暇耶
昔人嘗有言矣井田之制昉於黃唐備於
成周誠欲復之非數百年專力於此不可
雖使富民奉其田以爲井其勢亦不可得
===
此蘇氏之說也古之王者自治一國諸侯
亦各自治其國終歲以井田爲事今統一
天下吏數代易孰使爲之終無成效此葉
氏之說也然高祖雖不能復井田而能減
輕租稅孝文賜民田租之半孝武大修代
田之法王莽之末粟斛易一金光武之興
三十而稅一兩漢節儉至矣其法在李唐
者凡二變租庸調始於武德而成於貞觀
之時田雖不爲井而先王之意不失焉兩
punctuated: 人所掌，其法用助。商鞅決裂阡陌，田不井授，賦無定制，於是先王之迹熄，而兼并之勢成。漢高帝起，而悉去秦法。自今觀之，秦之虐政莫大於廢井田，漢之更化亦莫大於復井田也。亂極甫治，土曠寡民，可復而不復，是果啓導之無人，而經理之未暇耶？昔人嘗有言矣：井田之制昉於黃唐，備於成周。誠欲復之，非數百年專力於此不可。雖使富民奉其田以爲井，其勢亦不可得。此蘇氏之說也。古之王者自治一國，諸侯亦各自治其國，終歲以井田爲事。今統一天下，吏數代易，孰使爲之？終無成效。此葉氏之說也。然高祖雖不能復井田，而能減輕租稅。孝文賜民田租之半，孝武大修代田之法。王莽之末，粟斛易一金；光武之興，三十而稅一。兩漢節儉至矣。其法在李唐者凡二變：租庸調始於武德，而成於貞觀之時，田雖不爲井，而先王之意不失焉。兩
translation_en:
…under the charge of the Director of Works, and their method was collective cultivation of the public field as tax payment. Shang Yang broke up the field boundaries; land was no longer allotted in well-fields, and taxation had no fixed system. Thus the traces of the former kings vanished, and the tendency toward the concentration of landholdings took shape. Emperor Gao of Han arose and abolished all Qin institutions. Viewed from our own time, no oppressive policy of Qin was greater than its abolition of the well-field system; likewise, no reform under Han could have been greater than restoring it. As order was only just returning after extreme turmoil, with vast stretches of land and few inhabitants, restoration was possible, yet it was not undertaken. Was this really because no one offered guidance and there had been no time to organize it?

A writer of earlier times once said: “The well-field system began under the Yellow Emperor and Tang Yao and reached its full development under Zhou. Truly to restore it would require several hundred years of dedicated effort. Even if wealthy people offered their land to form well-fields, circumstances would still make it impossible.” This was Master Su’s argument. “The kings of antiquity personally governed a single state, and the regional lords likewise each governed their own states, attending to the well-fields throughout the year. Now the whole realm is unified, and officials are frequently replaced. Whom could one commission to carry this out? In the end, there would be no effective result.” This was Master Ye’s argument.

Yet although Gaozu could not restore the well-fields, he was able to reduce taxes. Emperor Xiaowen remitted half the people’s land tax, and Emperor Xiaowu greatly improved the alternating-field method of cultivation. At the end of Wang Mang’s rule, one hu of grain exchanged for one measure of gold; when Guangwu arose, the tax was one-thirtieth of the harvest. The two Han dynasties carried frugality to its utmost extent.

Under the Li house of Tang, the system underwent two changes. The system of grain tax, labor service or its commutation, and household levy began in the Wude reign and reached completion during the Zhenguan reign. Although the fields were not organized as well-fields, the intent of the former kings was preserved. The Two…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
稅定於楊炎而行於建中之初稅雖未爲
輕而租戶雜徭悉省焉陸贄諸人皆善租
庸調而不取兩稅然租庸調以下身爲本
其弊也多挾空籍以徼賦其變爲兩稅者
夫亦必至之勢乎兩稅以資產爲宗其弊
也不知任土以作貢其至於重困者豈非
有司之過乎宋田賦大抵襲唐其不善者
熙寧青苗之法以官之所有而取息於民
斂散出入吏緣爲奸所受者非其所欲也
淳熙改鈔之法以民之所入而追補於官
新故互易取民無制所償者非其所負也
===
我
朝經制立法莫不損益前代而分田定賦自
可垂法後王故官民之分助法之公田私
田也等則之差禹貢之則壤成賦也山澤
園廛之征周禮之衡虞夫里之入也絁絹
布縷之準亦周禮土宜辨物之事也下田
之徭秋夏之限唐之庸調兩稅之遺意也
punctuated:
稅定於楊炎而行於建中之初，稅雖未爲輕，而租戶雜徭悉省焉。陸贄諸人皆善租庸調而不取兩稅，然租庸調以下身爲本，其弊也，多挾空籍以徼賦。其變爲兩稅者，夫亦必至之勢乎？兩稅以資產爲宗，其弊也，不知任土以作貢。其至於重困者，豈非有司之過乎？宋田賦大抵襲唐，其不善者，熙寧青苗之法，以官之所有而取息於民，斂散出入，吏緣爲奸，所受者非其所欲也。淳熙改鈔之法，以民之所入而追補於官，新故互易，取民無制，所償者非其所負也。
我朝經制立法，莫不損益前代，而分田定賦，自可垂法後王。故官民之分，助法之公田私田也；等則之差，《禹貢》之則壤成賦也；山澤園廛之征，《周禮》之衡虞夫里之入也；絁絹布縷之準，亦《周禮》土宜辨物之事也；下田之徭、秋夏之限，唐之庸調兩稅之遺意也。
translation_en:
…the tax system was established by Yang Yan and implemented at the beginning of the Jianzhong reign period. Although taxation was still not light, the miscellaneous labor services imposed on rent-paying households were all abolished. Lu Zhi and others all approved of the grain-tax, labor-service, and textile-tax system (zu-yong-diao) and rejected the twice-yearly tax system. Yet the former system took the individual person as its basis [?]; its abuse lay in repeatedly using registers containing fictitious entries to exact taxes. Was its transformation into the twice-yearly tax system not, then, an inevitable development? The twice-yearly taxes took property as their basis. Their abuse lay in failing to assess tribute according to the productive capacity of the land. When this resulted in severe hardship, was it not the fault of the responsible officials?
Song land taxation largely followed Tang practice. Among its defective measures was the Green Sprouts scheme of the Xining reign period, which used government funds to extract interest from the people. In collecting and disbursing funds, officials exploited opportunities for fraud; what people received was not what they wanted. The note-exchange measure of the Chunxi reign period required supplementary payments to the government on what the people had paid in [?]. In exchanging old notes for new, exactions upon the people knew no limits; what they repaid was not what they owed.
In establishing institutions and laws, our dynasty has everywhere adapted the practices of preceding dynasties, retaining or modifying them as appropriate. Its classification of land and determination of taxes can indeed serve as a model for later sovereigns. Thus, the distinction between government and private land corresponds to the public and private fields of the ancient labor-assistance system (zhu). The differences in assessment grades correspond to determining taxes according to soil quality in the Tribute of Yu (Yu gong). Levies on mountains, marshes, gardens, and urban plots correspond to the revenues associated with the forest and marsh wardens and with agricultural holdings and residential plots in the Rites of Zhou (Zhou li). The standards for coarse silk, silk cloth, other cloth, and yarn likewise correspond to the Rites of Zhou’s differentiation of products according to what each locality is suited to produce. Labor-service obligations on lower-grade fields [?] and the autumn and summer deadlines preserve the intent of the Tang labor-service and textile taxes and its twice-yearly taxes.

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
行之一百六十年地不加少賦不加多勸農
之官常設而民愈以不紓催科之使四出
而課愈以不集海内皆然東南爲甚夫
國家經費多取給東南之民而西北一省不
足比東南之郡故曰江淮財賦之淵也又
曰江淮天下敖倉也柰何賈氏公田之遺
禍猶存而
國初沒官之租籍仍舊兼以水旱疫癘之爲
災積荒公占之爲累通融則甲及於乙增
===
耗或子浮於母
朝廷有時而赦之州縣踰時而徵之民視
詔令皆虛文而畏苛政如猛虎追呼逮繫旁連
支屬逋逃自鬻併捐墳墓東南小民已不
勝其困矣西北瘠鹵之地所産有限所應
無窮輸邊之擾養馬之累而又爲近習權
貴乞爲庄田科以子粒往往皆欲舍其田
以逃其生自稼穡以來未有如
今日小民之不樂其田者也其故何哉賦額
punctuated: 行之一百六十年，地不加少，賦不加多，勸農之官常設，而民愈以不紓；催科之使四出，而課愈以不集。海内皆然，東南爲甚。夫國家經費，多取給東南之民，而西北一省不足比東南之郡，故曰：「江淮，財賦之淵也。」又曰：「江淮，天下敖倉也。」柰何賈氏公田之遺禍猶存，而國初沒官之租籍仍舊，兼以水旱疫癘之爲災、積荒公占之爲累，通融則甲及於乙，增耗或子浮於母。朝廷有時而赦之，州縣踰時而徵之。民視詔令皆虛文，而畏苛政如猛虎。追呼逮繫，旁連支屬，逋逃自鬻，併捐墳墓，東南小民已不勝其困矣。西北瘠鹵之地，所産有限，所應無窮，輸邊之擾，養馬之累，而又爲近習權貴乞爲庄田，科以子粒，往往皆欲舍其田以逃其生。自稼穡以來，未有如今日小民之不樂其田者也。其故何哉？賦額
translation_en:
…These arrangements have been in force for one hundred and sixty years. The land has not diminished, nor have the taxes increased. Officials charged with encouraging agriculture are permanently appointed, yet the people find ever less relief; agents charged with pressing tax collection go out in every direction, yet the assessed revenues are ever less fully collected. This is so throughout the realm, but most acutely in the southeast. State expenditure is largely supplied by the people of the southeast: an entire northwestern province cannot match a single southeastern prefecture. Thus it is said, “The Jiang–Huai region is the wellspring of fiscal revenue,” and again, “The Jiang–Huai region is the Ao Granary of the realm.” Why, then, do the lingering evils of Jia’s public-field scheme remain, while the rent registers for lands confiscated at the beginning of our dynasty remain unchanged? Added to these are the disasters of flood, drought, and epidemic, and the burdens of accumulated wasteland and official encroachment. When liabilities are redistributed, one person’s burden falls upon another; when wastage surcharges are added, the supplementary levy may exceed the principal. The court sometimes remits these dues, but prefectures and counties collect them after their due dates have passed. The people regard imperial edicts as empty words and fear oppressive government as they would a ferocious tiger. Pursued with summonses, arrested, and imprisoned, with collateral relatives also implicated, they flee, sell themselves, and even abandon their ancestral graves. The common people of the southeast can no longer bear their distress.

In the northwest, where the soil is barren and saline, production is limited, but the demands to be met are endless. There are the disruptions of transporting supplies to the frontier and the burdens of raising horses. Moreover, imperial intimates and powerful dignitaries petition to have these lands made into estates and impose grain levies upon them. Again and again, the people wish to abandon their fields and flee to save their lives. Since cultivation first began, never have the common people taken so little pleasure in their fields as they do today. What is the reason? The tax quotas…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
之不均也兼并之未抑也今天下之田不
可井矣非惟不可井不可均矣非惟不可
均不可限矣然則如之何而後可不驚世
不惑衆其惟減額乎其惟均則乎易曰損
上益下其道大光減額之謂也又曰裒多
益寡稱物平施均則之謂也魏𨯳有言貪
賦而不愛人是虞人反裘而負薪徒惜其
毛不知皮盡而毛無所傅李渤有言聚斂
之徒剥下媚上惟思竭澤不慮無魚由此
===
觀之則知田額決不可以不減田則決不
可以不均也然減額非欲籍天下之田而
通減之減其當減之甚者如四斗以上八
斗以下甚至滿石或石以上者此在所必
減不減則古者什一今者什五科重者皆
歸之小民而又有額本輕而重者加於非
其額者乎均則亦非欲一天下之則而盡
均之均其不均之甚者如五升以下七斗
以上甚至無額或石以上者此在所必均
punctuated:
之不均也，兼并之未抑也。今天下之田不可井矣，非惟不可井，不可均矣；非惟不可均，不可限矣。然則如之何而後可？不驚世，不惑衆，其惟減額乎？其惟均則乎？《易》曰：「損上益下，其道大光。」減額之謂也。又曰：「裒多益寡，稱物平施。」均則之謂也。魏𨯳有言：「貪賦而不愛人，是虞人反裘而負薪，徒惜其毛，不知皮盡而毛無所傅。」李渤有言：「聚斂之徒，剥下媚上，惟思竭澤，不慮無魚。」由此觀之，則知田額決不可以不減，田則決不可以不均也。

然減額非欲籍天下之田而通減之，減其當減之甚者，如四斗以上八斗以下，甚至滿石或石以上者，此在所必減。不減，則古者什一，今者什五，科重者皆歸之小民，而又有額本輕而重者加於非其額者乎？均則亦非欲一天下之則而盡均之，均其不均之甚者，如五升以下七斗以上，甚至無額或石以上者，此在所必均。
translation_en:
…because the tax quotas are unequal and the concentration of landholdings has not been checked. Today, the land throughout the realm can no longer be organized under the well-field system. Not only can it not be organized into well-fields; it cannot even be distributed equally. Not only can it not be distributed equally; limits cannot even be imposed on holdings. What, then, can be done? To avoid alarming the world or unsettling the multitude, surely the answer lies in reducing quotas and equalizing assessment rates? The Book of Changes says: “Diminish what is above and increase what is below: this way shines greatly.” This speaks to reducing quotas. It also says: “Take from the plentiful and supplement the scant; weigh things and distribute impartially.” This speaks to equalizing assessment rates. Wei Zheng [?; transcribed 魏𨯳] said: “To covet taxes without caring for the people is like a forester carrying firewood with his fur coat turned inside out. He merely cherishes the fur, unaware that once the hide is worn away, the fur will have nothing to adhere to.” Li Bo said: “Those who exact wealth strip those below to flatter those above. They think only of draining the marsh, without considering that no fish will remain.” Viewed in this light, land-tax quotas absolutely must be reduced, and land-tax assessment rates absolutely must be equalized.

Yet reducing quotas does not mean registering all the land in the realm and reducing its quotas across the board. It means reducing the most extreme quotas that ought to be reduced: for example, those of four to eight dou, or even a full shi or more. These must be reduced. Otherwise, whereas in antiquity the tax was one-tenth, today it is five-tenths, with all the heavy assessments falling upon the common people. And are there not also cases in which the original quota is light, yet heavier charges are added beyond that quota? Equalizing assessment rates likewise does not mean imposing a single rate throughout the realm and making every assessment identical. It means correcting the most extreme inequalities: for example, rates of five sheng or less alongside those of seven dou or more, or even no quota at all alongside quotas of more than one shi. These must be equalized.…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
不均則民者何事官者何事知重者皆小
民佃之而又有興本非重而輕者移於非
其則者乎若謂經用有數額不可減殊不
知計經用而減之節其冗費汰其冗食有
不知其減矣
先朝嘗一行焉撫臣有周文襄而輔臣楊文貞
實贊成之也若謂物情不齊則不可均殊
不知因物情而均之辨其高下類其肥瘠
有不難於均矣近時嘗一試焉東南之湖
===
州西北大名諸郡實興起者也苟得其人
以專其委任以無拘其文法減額先其沒
官之科以比於輕不得已而稍重焉均則
去其畸零之數以歸於一不得已而爲二
焉則必有如李安世之於元魏朱元晦之
於漳州必無不可行者賦額既均無幷自
抑百姓既足儲峙自充先王之治可復覩
也且天無常時地無常利物盛則衰時極
而轉禹貢揚州之域厥田下下其穀宜稻
punctuated:
不均，則民者何事，官者何事？知重者皆小民佃之，而又有興本非重而輕者移於非其則者乎？若謂經用有數，額不可減，殊不知計經用而減之，節其冗費，汰其冗食，有不知其減矣。先朝嘗一行焉，撫臣有周文襄，而輔臣楊文貞實贊成之也。若謂物情不齊，則不可均，殊不知因物情而均之，辨其高下，類其肥瘠，有不難於均矣。近時嘗一試焉，東南之湖州、西北大名諸郡，實興起者也。

苟得其人，以專其委任，以無拘其文法，減額先其沒官之科，以比於輕，不得已而稍重焉；均則去其畸零之數，以歸於一，不得已而爲二焉。則必有如李安世之於元魏、朱元晦之於漳州，必無不可行者。賦額既均，無幷自抑，百姓既足，儲峙自充，先王之治可復覩也。且天無常時，地無常利，物盛則衰，時極而轉。《禹貢》揚州之域，厥田下下，其穀宜稻。
translation_en:
…If the rates are not equalized, what are the common people to do, and what are the officials to do? We know that the heavily taxed lands are all cultivated by ordinary tenant farmers; might there also be cases in which burdens originally light rather than heavy have been shifted to a rate not properly applicable to them [?]? If it is argued that regular expenditure has a fixed amount and tax quotas therefore cannot be reduced, this entirely overlooks the possibility of calculating regular expenditure and making reductions accordingly. Curtail superfluous expenses and eliminate those needlessly maintained at public expense, and the reduction can pass unnoticed. This was once carried out in a former reign: among the grand coordinators was Zhou Wenxiang, and the grand secretary Yang Wenzhen actively supported its accomplishment. If it is argued that circumstances differ and rates therefore cannot be equalized, this entirely overlooks the possibility of equalizing them according to those circumstances. Distinguish high-lying from low-lying land and classify it by fertility or barrenness, and equalization need not be difficult. This has recently been tried: Huzhou in the southeast and Daming and other prefectures in the northwest have indeed taken the initiative.

If suitable men are found, entrusted with full responsibility, and freed from restrictive administrative rules, then, in reducing quotas, they should begin with the assessments on lands confiscated by the government, bringing them into line with lighter assessments and allowing somewhat heavier ones only where unavoidable. In equalizing rates, they should eliminate irregular fractional amounts and consolidate them into a single rate, allowing two only where unavoidable. There will surely then be men like Li Anshi under the Northern Wei or Zhu Yuanhui in Zhangzhou, and nothing about these measures need prove impracticable. Once tax quotas have been equalized, engrossment of land will naturally be checked [?]; once the people have enough, reserves will naturally be replenished. The government of the ancient kings may once again be seen. Moreover, Heaven has no unchanging seasons, and the earth yields no unchanging benefits. When things flourish, they then decline; when an age reaches its extreme, it turns. In the domain of Yangzhou described in the Tribute of Yu, the fields were ranked lowest of the low, and rice was the grain suited to them…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
漢楚及隋戶賦之數裁及天下四分之一
耳至唐則所出居十九至宋則轉漕三百
萬其盛莫加焉
今日東南民力之困安知地利不復如三代
漢晉隋之時乎此又謀國者所當審觀而
蚤圖之也愚也家素力田目擊斯弊有懷
欲吐久矣傳曰狂夫之言聖人擇焉願執
事不罪其狂而轉之于
上
===
第五問
張珩
同考試官學正吳　批〔泛古人物其流風餘韻振人耳目者至今猶存此策考據精詳文詞爾雅且以文章節義〕
〔二者本之道學所謂體用一原者固如是豈當與仰止之懷〕
〔者歟〕
考試官主事屠　批〔題本浩繁作者類多支蔓暢而有叙僅見此篇〕
考試官署郎中盧　批〔得御事體〕
punctuated:
漢楚及隋，戶賦之數裁及天下四分之一耳。至唐，則所出居十九；至宋，則轉漕三百萬，其盛莫加焉。今日東南民力之困，安知地利不復如三代、漢、晉、隋之時乎？此又謀國者所當審觀而蚤圖之也。愚也家素力田，目擊斯弊，有懷欲吐久矣。傳曰：「狂夫之言，聖人擇焉。」願執事不罪其狂，而轉之于上。

第五問
張珩
同考試官學正吳　批〔泛古人物，其流風餘韻振人耳目者，至今猶存。此策考據精詳，文詞爾雅，且以文章節義〕〔二者本之道學，所謂體用一原者固如是。豈當與仰止之懷〕〔者歟？〕
考試官主事屠　批〔題本浩繁，作者類多支蔓，暢而有叙，僅見此篇。〕
考試官署郎中盧　批〔得御事體。〕
translation_en:
…Under Han, Chu [?], and Sui, the household tax revenue amounted to only one quarter of the empire’s total. By the Tang, however, the region supplied nine tenths; by the Song, its grain shipments amounted to three million. Its prosperity could scarcely have been greater.

Given the present exhaustion of the people’s resources in the southeast, how do we know that the land’s productivity has not reverted to what it was under the Three Dynasties, Han, Jin, and Sui? This, too, is something those who plan for the state should examine carefully and make provision for early. My family has always worked diligently at farming, and I have witnessed these abuses myself. I have long wished to express what is in my heart. A transmitted text says: “Even in a madman’s words, the sage finds something to adopt.” I hope that you will not condemn my rashness, but will convey these words to His Majesty.

Fifth Question
Zhang Heng

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, School Director: 〔Among figures of antiquity [?], the enduring influence and lingering resonance that enliven people’s eyes and ears remain to this day. This policy essay is precise and detailed in its examination of evidence, and its language is elegant and correct. Moreover, it roots both literary achievement and moral integrity〕〔in the Learning of the Way. This is indeed what is meant by “substance and function have a single source.” Could it appropriately inspire feelings of reverent admiration〕〔[?]?〕

Comment by Examiner Tu, Secretary: 〔The question itself is extensive and complex, and most writers stray into excessive ramifications. Only this essay is both fluent and orderly.〕

Comment by Examiner Lu, Acting Director: 〔It grasps the proper manner of managing affairs [?].〕

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖學務其全而凡以一行名者斯偏矣論
人欲其盡而凡以一善拘者斯畧矣是故
儒者無一偏之學君子大擇善之功必求
其內外之兼濟本末之並茂而后謂之全
觀其才德之互勝文行之相孚而后謂之
盡知此則所以論天下之士者裕矣而況
江右之産乎執事有見于道學節義文章
之異而謂士之品有三愚竊以爲士之品
一而已耳道學其原也節義者道學之見
===
諸行而文章者道學之修諸言也夫茍道
學之有得矣則見乎外者明白而俊偉因
時而節義著焉宣之言者正大而光明隨
事而文章形焉然則執事所謂三者果異
乎同也執事終有疑于道學之易節義之
難而謂文章之尤難愚竊以爲今之所謂
道學者非古矣相沿于口耳見聞之末而
無益乎身心誦說于先儒講明之后而掩
襲其糟粕然則道學何貴也故民俗日偷
punctuated:
聖學務其全，而凡以一行名者斯偏矣；論人欲其盡，而凡以一善拘者斯畧矣。是故儒者無一偏之學，君子大擇善之功，必求其內外之兼濟、本末之並茂，而后謂之全；觀其才德之互勝、文行之相孚，而后謂之盡。知此，則所以論天下之士者裕矣，而況江右之産乎？
執事有見于道學、節義、文章之異，而謂士之品有三。愚竊以爲士之品一而已耳：道學其原也，節義者道學之見諸行，而文章者道學之修諸言也。夫茍道學之有得矣，則見乎外者明白而俊偉，因時而節義著焉；宣之言者正大而光明，隨事而文章形焉。然則執事所謂三者，果異乎？同也。
執事終有疑于道學之易、節義之難，而謂文章之尤難。愚竊以爲今之所謂道學者非古矣：相沿于口耳見聞之末，而無益乎身心；誦說于先儒講明之后，而掩襲其糟粕。然則道學何貴也？故民俗日偷
translation_en:
The learning of the sages seeks completeness; anyone known for a single form of conduct is therefore partial. In judging people, one seeks a full assessment; any judgment confined to a single virtue is therefore cursory. Thus the Confucian scholar’s learning is never one-sided, and the gentleman esteems the work of choosing what is good [?]. Only when the inward and outward are both fulfilled, and root and branches flourish together, can this be called completeness. Only after observing how a person’s abilities and virtue each excel, and how his writing and conduct accord with one another, can an assessment be called full. Knowing this, one has ample means to judge the scholars of the realm—how much more so those born in Jiangyou!
You, honored examiners, perceive differences between Learning of the Way, moral integrity and righteousness, and literary composition, and therefore say that scholars fall into three categories. I humbly submit that there is only one category of scholar. Learning of the Way is its source: integrity and righteousness are Learning of the Way manifested in conduct, while literary composition is Learning of the Way cultivated in words. If one has truly attained something in Learning of the Way, its outward manifestations will be clear and outstanding, and integrity and righteousness will become evident as circumstances call for them. What one expresses in words will be upright and luminous, and literary composition will take shape in response to particular affairs. Are the three things you speak of, then, really different? They are one.
You nevertheless harbor doubts concerning the ease of Learning of the Way and the difficulty of integrity and righteousness, and maintain that literary composition is harder still. I humbly submit that what is now called Learning of the Way is no longer what it was in antiquity. People perpetuate the superficial business of what passes from mouth to ear and what is seen and heard, without benefiting their own persons and minds. They recite and expound what earlier Confucian scholars have already elucidated, covertly appropriating their dregs. What, then, is there to esteem in such Learning of the Way? Hence popular customs grow daily more lax…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
士風不振而節義寡矣誇多眩博剽古襲
奇而文體陋矣然則執事之以爲易者果
易乎否也夫道學之名后世始著而在于
江右有可言者陳文蔚著書立言遵師說
而不變彭龜年愛君憂國觸時忌而益堅
是固篤信好學者也若楊萬里知誠意正
心之說而不以掖垣易一記斯可謂仁者
之勇矣尹天民恐爲顏閔所笑而不因好
官見時宰斯可謂中立不倚矣隱居講道
===
德性是尊者非陸九淵兄弟乎究義利之
歸而聞者泣下非有德之言不能也著荆
門之政而士民心服豈徒務虛名而無實
用者哉因陳番問易無定體之旨而來楊
震天下后世儒宗之稱者非張邈乎當漢
室之季道學未明而深究大易之旨雖陳
蕃楊震世稱鳳儒而有推尊之言則其聞
道可知矣丈八是諸子者雖其餘言遺行紀
載所不能詳而立心制行皆有非后世所
punctuated: 士風不振，而節義寡矣；誇多眩博，剽古襲奇，而文體陋矣。然則執事之以爲易者，果易乎？否也。夫道學之名，后世始著，而在于江右，有可言者。陳文蔚著書立言，遵師說而不變；彭龜年愛君憂國，觸時忌而益堅，是固篤信好學者也。若楊萬里知誠意正心之說，而不以掖垣易一記，斯可謂仁者之勇矣。尹天民恐爲顏閔所笑，而不因好官見時宰，斯可謂中立不倚矣。隱居講道，德性是尊者，非陸九淵兄弟乎？究義利之歸，而聞者泣下，非有德之言不能也。著荆門之政，而士民心服，豈徒務虛名而無實用者哉？因陳番問《易》無定體之旨，而來楊震「天下后世儒宗」之稱者，非張邈乎？當漢室之季，道學未明，而深究《大易》之旨，雖陳蕃、楊震，世稱鳳儒，而有推尊之言，則其聞道可知矣。丈八是諸子者，雖其餘言遺行，紀載所不能詳，而立心制行，皆有非后世所
translation_en:
…the ethos of scholars fails to flourish, and integrity and righteousness are scarce. They boast of their extensive learning and dazzle others with their erudition, pilfering from antiquity and copying the unusual, while their literary style grows debased. Is what you, sir, regard as easy truly easy, then? No.

The name “Learning of the Way” became prominent only in later ages, and there are practitioners in Jiangyou worth discussing. Chen Wenwei wrote books and expounded his views, adhering unwaveringly to his teacher’s teachings. Peng Guinian loved his sovereign and cared deeply for his country; the more he offended the taboos of his time, the firmer he became. These were certainly men of steadfast faith and devotion to learning. Yang Wanli understood the teaching of making one’s intentions sincere and rectifying one’s mind, and would not exchange a single commemorative essay for a post in the imperial drafting offices [?]. This may be called the courage of the benevolent. Yin Tianmin feared being laughed at by Yan Hui and Min Sun, and would not seek an audience with the chief minister of his day for the sake of a fine official post. This may be called standing firm in the middle without leaning to either side.

Were those who lived in retirement, taught the Way, and honored their moral nature not Lu Jiuyuan and his brothers? He investigated the ultimate implications of righteousness and profit, bringing his listeners to tears: only the words of a man of virtue could accomplish this. His administration at Jingmen was distinguished, and scholars and commoners submitted to him wholeheartedly. Could he have been someone who merely pursued an empty reputation without practical efficacy?

Was it not Zhang Miao [?] who, through Chen Fan’s question about the meaning of the Changes having no fixed form, elicited Yang Zhen’s praise as “a master of Confucian learning for all the world and later generations”? In the closing years of the Han house, when the Learning of the Way had not yet been clearly elucidated, he probed deeply into the meaning of the Great Changes. Even Chen Fan and Yang Zhen, acclaimed in their age as “phoenix scholars” [?], spoke of him with reverence; from this we can understand his grasp of the Way. [Unclear characters: 丈八.] These masters, though the records cannot fully detail their surviving words and deeds, all possessed qualities in the formation of their intentions and the regulation of their conduct that later generations could not…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
可及者惟不能會聖道之大成而徇吾心
之獨得是以尊德性者或失之內而尊所
聞者或失之外耳節義之名因時始見而
其在宋尤有可言洪皓使金留十五年不
屈可謂宋之蘇武矣而子遵復以死正數
國之禮卓乎臨大節而不可奪者歟曾𢛳
被執不屈越城可謂宋之顏真卿矣而孫
悟復罵賊死于臺州偉然可以寄百里之
命者歟抱印登城而死戰報國黃從善之
===
守死弗去也責卜市肆而慟哭以卒謝枋
得固無所爲而爲善者哉李成大謀復金
壇遇寇不屈而二子亦以徇節死焉其所
謂子爲父死臣爲君死者可謂能濟其美
矣文天祥就刑燕市舉動不渝其自贊孔
曰成仁孟曰取義者非所謂欲仁得仁者
哉若漢之徐穉超世遺俗臣得危邦不入
之義而晉之陶潛隱居不仕可謂不懷二
心者矣由是觀之惟穉之未仕爲臣故可
punctuated: 可及者。惟不能會聖道之大成，而徇吾心之獨得，是以尊德性者或失之內，而尊所聞者或失之外耳。節義之名，因時始見，而其在宋尤有可言。洪皓使金，留十五年不屈，可謂宋之蘇武矣；而子遵復以死正數國之禮，卓乎臨大節而不可奪者歟！曾𢛳被執，不屈越城，可謂宋之顏真卿矣；而孫悟復罵賊，死于臺州，偉然可以寄百里之命者歟！抱印登城，而死戰報國，黃從善之守死弗去也。責卜市肆，而慟哭以卒，謝枋得固無所爲而爲善者哉！李成大謀復金壇，遇寇不屈，而二子亦以徇節死焉。其所謂子爲父死、臣爲君死者，可謂能濟其美矣。文天祥就刑燕市，舉動不渝，其自贊「孔曰成仁，孟曰取義」者，非所謂欲仁得仁者哉！若漢之徐穉，超世遺俗，臣得危邦不入之義；而晉之陶潛，隱居不仕，可謂不懷二心者矣。由是觀之，惟穉之未仕爲臣，故可
translation_en:
…could equal. Yet they could not comprehend the full culmination of the sages’ Way, instead following the insights individually attained in their own minds. Thus those who honored their moral nature sometimes erred by turning too far inward, while those who honored what they had learned sometimes erred by turning too far outward.

A reputation for integrity and righteousness becomes manifest only when circumstances call it forth, and the Song offers particularly noteworthy examples. Hong Hao went as an envoy to the Jin and was detained for fifteen years without yielding; he may be called the Su Wu of the Song. His son Zun, in turn, upheld proper diplomatic ceremonial [?] at the cost of his life. How outstanding—a man whose resolve could not be shaken when confronted with a great moral test! Zeng [?] (曾𢛳) was captured and refused to yield at Yuecheng; he may be called the Yan Zhenqing of the Song. His grandson Wu, in turn, cursed the rebels and died at Taizhou. How admirable—a man to whom the lives of the people of a hundred-li domain could be entrusted!

Clasping his official seal, he mounted the city wall and fought to the death to repay his country: such was Huang Congshan’s resolve to hold his post until death and never leave. Practicing divination [?] in the marketplace, he wept bitterly until he died: surely Xie Fangde was one who did good without seeking anything in return! Li Chengda planned to recover Jintan and, when he encountered the rebels, refused to yield; his two sons likewise died for their principles. In exemplifying the saying that a son dies for his father and a minister dies for his ruler, they may be said to have brought this virtue to fulfillment.

Wen Tianxiang went to his execution in the marketplace of Yan, unwavering in his conduct. In his own encomium he wrote, “Confucius spoke of fulfilling benevolence; Mencius spoke of choosing righteousness.” Was he not one of those described as seeking benevolence and attaining it? As for Xu Zhi of the Han, he rose above the world and abandoned its conventions, grasping [?] the principle of not entering a state in peril. Tao Qian of the Jin lived in retirement and declined office; he may be said to have harbored no divided allegiance. Viewed in this light, it was precisely because Xu Zhi had not taken office as a minister that he could…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
行其潔身之義而潛之上下無交惟可遂
其箕山之節耳若宋之謝臣則皆膺專閫
之寄受天子之命其舍生以取義不亦當
乎要不可以生死之異而疑其節義之殊
也夫是數子者或得于涵養之既深或出
于天資之近道雖其志與日月爭光而
論其行與金石不朽此正氣在天地彝倫
在人心而所以為道學者固不外此也又
豈可以優劣觀乎若文章之在人斯可論
===
矣曾鞏見稱于史氏謂其斟酌司馬遷韓
愈之善李覯論薦于范仲淹謂其立言有
孟軻楊雄之風固皆足以成一家之言也
若歐陽修文章復古起五代相沿之習而
韻鏗鏘一蹴來可與第一之稱則可謂
名世之文矣黃庭堅謫為奇古特立萬物
之表固也而其游戲之習殆所謂本之則
無者歟王安石文高一世尤以道德經濟
為己任固也而其偏拗之行殆亦學術之
punctuated: 行其潔身之義，而潛之上下無交，惟可遂其箕山之節耳。若宋之謝臣，則皆膺專閫之寄，受天子之命，其舍生以取義，不亦當乎？要不可以生死之異而疑其節義之殊也。夫是數子者，或得于涵養之既深，或出于天資之近道，雖其志與日月爭光，而論其行，與金石不朽。此正氣在天地，彝倫在人心，而所以為道學者，固不外此也，又豈可以優劣觀乎？若文章之在人，斯可論矣。曾鞏見稱于史氏，謂其斟酌司馬遷、韓愈之善；李覯論薦于范仲淹，謂其立言有孟軻、楊雄之風，固皆足以成一家之言也。若歐陽修文章復古，起五代相沿之習，而韻鏗鏘一蹴來可與第一之稱，則可謂名世之文矣。黃庭堅謫為奇古，特立萬物之表，固也；而其游戲之習，殆所謂本之則無者歟？王安石文高一世，尤以道德經濟為己任，固也；而其偏拗之行，殆亦學術之
translation_en:
…carry out his duty to preserve his own integrity, whereas Tao Qian, having no dealings with those above or below him, could only fulfill his commitment to the integrity exemplified by the recluse of Mount Ji. As for the Song ministers designated here as “Xie” [?], all had been entrusted with independent military commands and had received the Son of Heaven’s mandate. Was it not fitting that they should sacrifice their lives to uphold righteousness? In any event, differences in whether they lived or died should not lead us to doubt that their integrity and righteousness were alike. These men attained this either through profound and sustained self-cultivation or through natural endowments close to the Way. Their aspirations rivaled the sun and moon in brilliance; as for their deeds, these endure like metal and stone. This is the upright vital force within Heaven and Earth, and the enduring moral relationships within the human heart. What constitutes the Learning of the Way certainly lies within these things. How, then, could we rank them as superior or inferior?

People’s literary achievements, however, do admit of evaluation. Zeng Gong was praised by the historians, who said that he judiciously drew upon the strengths of Sima Qian and Han Yu. Li Gou was commended and recommended by Fan Zhongyan, who said that his writings had the manner of Meng Ke and Yang Xiong. Both were certainly capable of establishing distinctive bodies of thought in their writings. Ouyang Xiu restored antiquity in literary composition, rising above the conventions handed down from the Five Dynasties; his rhythms rang out sonorously, and he could at a single stride receive the designation “foremost” [?]. His writings may thus be called works that brought renown to their age. Huang Tingjian’s [poetry?] was indeed unusual and archaic, standing uniquely beyond all things. Yet his habit of literary play was perhaps what is meant by “when one seeks its foundation, there is nothing”—was it not? Wang Anshi’s writing surpassed that of his contemporaries, and he particularly took moral principle and statecraft as his own responsibility: this is certainly so. Yet his wayward and obstinate conduct was perhaps also a consequence of his learning’s…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
偏故與夫是諸子者或因文而見道或務
末而遺本故明有所照則文章可觀而知
識未融則躬行不逮固理之常耳若明問
之所未及豈無人哉布澤懷遠精于吏事
者陶侃也所謂機動明鑑似魏武忠順勤
勞似孔明者非確論乎志尚高潔剛正不
移者劉濞也所謂文章似司馬遷而遷無
其風節風節似疏廣受而廣受無其文學
者非其人乎奮不顧身決定大計則有趙
===
汝愚焉進賢用能輔成君德則有晏殊焉
是諸子者或文學之優或節義之著可謂
無忝前人矣傳不云乎太上立德其次立
功其次立言諸君子者道學足以希賢節
義足以經世文章足以憲古要之皆爲不
朽固非后學可輕議也然要而論之道學
之在人猶木之有本歟節義其質幹也文
章其枝葉也使釋其本而末之求焉則雖
婺結纓之死自謂見危授命而卒以稱
punctuated:
偏故與？夫是諸子者，或因文而見道，或務末而遺本。故明有所照，則文章可觀；而知識未融，則躬行不逮，固理之常耳。若明問之所未及，豈無人哉？布澤懷遠，精于吏事者，陶侃也。所謂機動明鑑似魏武，忠順勤勞似孔明者，非確論乎？志尚高潔，剛正不移者，劉濞也。所謂文章似司馬遷，而遷無其風節；風節似疏廣、受，而廣、受無其文學者，非其人乎？奮不顧身，決定大計，則有趙汝愚焉；進賢用能，輔成君德，則有晏殊焉。是諸子者，或文學之優，或節義之著，可謂無忝前人矣。
傳不云乎：「太上立德，其次立功，其次立言。」諸君子者，道學足以希賢，節義足以經世，文章足以憲古，要之皆爲不朽，固非后學可輕議也。然要而論之，道學之在人，猶木之有本歟？節義，其質幹也；文章，其枝葉也。使釋其本而末之求焉，則雖婺結纓之死，自謂見危授命，而卒以稱
translation_en:
…the result of a bias in his learning, was it not? These masters either perceived the Way through writing or pursued the peripheral and neglected the fundamental. Thus, where their understanding illuminated something, their writings were worthy of admiration; where their knowledge had not become fully integrated, their personal conduct fell short. This is surely only the ordinary course of things. As for those whom your discerning question has not mentioned, could there be none? It was Tao Kan who spread beneficence, won over distant peoples, and excelled in administrative affairs. Was it not an accurate judgment to say that his resourcefulness and clear discernment resembled those of Wei Wudi, while his loyalty, obedience, diligence, and toil resembled those of Kongming? It was Liu Bi [?] whose aspirations were lofty and pure, and who remained unshakably upright. Was he not the man of whom it was said that his writing resembled Sima Qian’s, yet Qian lacked his moral integrity; and that his moral integrity resembled that of Shu Guang and Shu Shou, yet Guang and Shou lacked his literary learning? For resolute action without regard for personal safety and the determination of great affairs, there was Zhao Ruyu; for advancing the worthy, employing the capable, and helping perfect the ruler’s virtue, there was Yan Shu. These masters, distinguished either by literary learning or by integrity and righteousness, may be said to have brought no dishonor upon their predecessors.
Does not the Commentary say: “Highest is establishing virtue; next is establishing meritorious deeds; next is establishing enduring words”? These gentlemen’s learning of the Way was sufficient to aspire to worthiness; their integrity and righteousness were sufficient to bring order to the world; and their writing was sufficient to take antiquity as its model. In sum, all achieved enduring renown, and certainly cannot be lightly judged by later students. Yet, to state the essential point, is not a person’s learning of the Way like the roots of a tree? Integrity and righteousness are its trunk; writing is its branches and leaves. If one abandons the root and seeks only the extremities, then even the death of Wu [?], tying his cap strings, which he himself considered giving his life in the face of danger, would ultimately be called…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
勇矣東漢黨錮諸賢自謂不變塞焉而卒
以敗事矣是求爲節義而未明所處者也
相如封禪之作窮極典故而失之誣天子
雲美新之文用意宏深而失之黨寇是固
以文章名而反以自累者也諸生誦道學
之言久矣竊有志而未能焉先賢在上文
獻具存寧不於文山諸君子而起敬
punctuated:
勇矣。東漢黨錮諸賢，自謂不變塞焉，而卒以敗事矣。是求爲節義而未明所處者也。相如封禪之作，窮極典故，而失之誣天；子雲美新之文，用意宏深，而失之黨寇。是固以文章名，而反以自累者也。
諸生誦道學之言久矣，竊有志而未能焉。先賢在上，文獻具存，寧不於文山諸君子而起敬？
translation_en:
…bravery. The worthies proscribed during the Eastern Han considered themselves unwavering in adversity [?], yet ultimately brought their undertaking to ruin. These were men who sought to uphold integrity and righteousness without clearly understanding their circumstances. Xiangru’s composition on the Feng and Shan sacrifices drew exhaustively upon classical precedents, yet erred in making false representations to Heaven; Ziyun’s essay Praising the Xin Dynasty was expansive and profound in intent, yet erred in siding with a usurper. These men certainly won fame through their writing, but instead brought reproach upon themselves through it.
We students have long recited the teachings of the Learning of the Way. We humbly aspire to follow them but have not yet succeeded. The worthies of earlier times stand above us, and their writings and records remain fully preserved. How could we fail to feel reverence for Wenshan and these other gentlemen?

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
皇上招選俊良翼翼我嘉靖既七年于
茲爰網廷議新舉試之法矣臣
襄臣應埈寔受
命有事江西時則相顧愕曰艱哉偲
偲乎責之重也惟誠有孚惟公
罔攸睹其慎而已廼暑月南下
===
比秋入其郊濟彭蠡瞻匡廬則
又顧謂曰偉哉恢恢乎壯而靈
也其入顧弗秀乎既入其境廼
御史〔良材〕而下揆物班事靡敢
不恪則又顧舂曰諒哉休休乎
體
上志也亡弗奮庸而承德乎廼預士
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

皇上招選俊良，翼翼我嘉靖既七年于茲，爰網廷議，新舉試之法矣。臣襄、臣應埈寔受命有事江西，時則相顧愕曰：「艱哉！偲偲乎責之重也！惟誠有孚，惟公罔攸睹，其慎而已。」廼暑月南下，比秋入其郊，濟彭蠡，瞻匡廬，則又顧謂曰：「偉哉！恢恢乎壯而靈也！其入顧弗秀乎？」既入其境，廼御史〔良材〕而下，揆物班事，靡敢不恪，則又顧舂曰：「諒哉！休休乎體上志也！亡弗奮庸而承德乎？」廼預士
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

His Majesty recruits and selects men of outstanding ability and virtue. With reverent diligence, our Jiajing reign has now reached its seventh year. Drawing upon deliberations at court [?], he has renewed the rules for selecting candidates through examination. Your servants Xiang and Yingjun duly received the command to conduct the examination in Jiangxi. We then looked at one another in consternation and said: “How difficult! How much mutual exhortation this weighty responsibility demands! Only sincerity inspires trust; only impartiality admits no regard for particular persons. We must simply exercise care.”

We accordingly traveled south in the summer months and reached the outskirts in autumn. Crossing Pengli and gazing upon Kuanglu, we again turned to one another and said: “How magnificent! How vast, majestic, and numinous! Could its people [?] possibly fail to be outstanding?” Once we had entered the territory, the Investigating Censor 〔Liangcai〕 and all those below him assessed requirements and assigned duties; none dared be remiss. We then turned to one another and said [?]: “How true-hearted! How generously they embody His Majesty’s intentions! Does not everyone exert himself in service to requite the imperial virtue?” Then we took part in examining the candidates …

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
所試而終閱之曰確而周知精
義矣紆而弗踈麗而則知言矣
斂而斷正而能濟可與謀矣義
精則達知言則明可與謀則穀
是弗當舉乎于是舉者九十五
人而簡錄其文以
獻臣應埈叙其末曰若古鄉士之
===
選不惟其途
國家采酌並用然卒重科目矣至
是
命廷臣司試事蓋視昔益慎云則與
茲舉者自視愈弗可輕也夫士
之處世惇節高議戚戚焉有不
逮用之憂比其用也庸有罔功
punctuated:
所試而終閱之，曰：「確而周，知精義矣；紆而弗踈，麗而則，知言矣；斂而斷，正而能濟，可與謀矣。義精則達，知言則明，可與謀則穀，是弗當舉乎？」于是舉者九十五人，而簡錄其文以獻。
臣應埈叙其末曰：「若古鄉士之選，不惟其途。國家采酌並用，然卒重科目矣。至是，命廷臣司試事，蓋視昔益慎云。則與茲舉者，自視愈弗可輕也。夫士之處世，惇節高議，戚戚焉有不逮用之憂；比其用也，庸有罔功
translation_en:
…what the candidates had written for the examination, and, having read it through, said: “Firm and comprehensive: they know how to refine their understanding of right principles. Expansive without looseness, elegant yet conforming to standards: they understand language. Restrained yet decisive, upright yet capable of accomplishing things: they can be consulted in deliberation. Refined understanding of principles brings penetration; understanding language brings clarity; fitness for deliberation brings good results. Should these men not be selected?” Accordingly, ninety-five men were selected, and a selection of their writings was transcribed for presentation to the throne.
Your servant Yingjun appends this postscript: “In antiquity, the selection of scholars from the local communities did not follow a single route. Our dynasty has considered and adopted these various methods together, yet ultimately places greatest weight on the examinations. Now court officials have been commanded to oversee the examination, showing still greater care than formerly. Those selected on this occasion must therefore take their own responsibilities all the more seriously. When scholars live in the world, they cultivate integrity and advance lofty arguments, anxiously fearing that they will never obtain employment. Yet when they are employed, there are some who accomplish nothing…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
者矣諸士固明揚待用者也其
嘗懷所以自見者乎行而違其
言曰儉有初而罔終曰悖二者
非君子所有也故體用內外一
而已厚積者昌本固斯茂君子
之學培其中而蒞物裕矣士罔
不欲爲君子者而或儉以悖何
也夫可欲斯誘矣畏斯葸矣艱
斯挫矣易斯忽矣偏執而弗化
斯劘矣時可進而務趨斯蕩矣
志眩于中而守喪于外豈其才
之罪哉是故仕以行道非干潤
也以惠民非擇位也易履而志
同異授而自任重凡以無愧焉
punctuated: 者矣。諸士固明揚待用者也，其嘗懷所以自見者乎？行而違其言曰儉，有初而罔終曰悖，二者非君子所有也。故體用內外一而已。厚積者昌，本固斯茂。君子之學，培其中而蒞物裕矣。士罔不欲爲君子者，而或儉以悖，何也？夫可欲斯誘矣，畏斯葸矣，艱斯挫矣，易斯忽矣，偏執而弗化斯劘矣，時可進而務趨斯蕩矣。志眩于中而守喪于外，豈其才之罪哉？是故仕以行道，非干潤也；以惠民，非擇位也。易履而志同，異授而自任重，凡以無愧焉
translation_en:
…those who accomplish nothing. You scholars are indeed men publicly commended for your worth and awaiting appointment. Have you ever considered how you will prove yourselves? To act contrary to one’s words is called falling short [?]; to begin but fail to carry through is called perversity. Neither belongs to the gentleman. Thus substance and application, the inward and the outward, are one. Those who accumulate deeply flourish; when the roots are firm, growth is abundant. The gentleman’s learning cultivates what is within, leaving him amply equipped to handle affairs. No scholar fails to wish to become a gentleman; why, then, do some fall short [?] and act perversely?

What is desirable entices them; what they fear makes them timid; difficulty discourages them; ease makes them careless. Clinging to one-sided views without adapting wears them down [?]; when the time permits advancement, striving to rush ahead leads them astray. Their purpose becomes confused within, and their steadfastness is lost in outward conduct. Can this be blamed on their abilities? Thus one takes office to put the Way into practice, not to seek material gain; to benefit the people, not to pick a desirable position. Though one’s circumstances change, one’s purpose remains the same; though appointments differ, one takes weighty responsibilities upon oneself—all so as to have nothing of which to be ashamed…

title: 嘉靖七年江西鄉試錄
text:
耳今夫楩楠梓杞諸木之良也
工師者擇焉樣稱宇棟隨所受
無弗當者夫人懷實入市而棄
之中衢曰凡以眩人而已顧不
大惑矣乎詩曰藹藹王多吉士
惟君子使媚于天子又曰藹藹
王多吉人惟君子命媚于庶人
言吉人之用而宜也諸士勗哉
===
刑部貴州清吏司主事屠應埈
謹序
punctuated:
耳。今夫楩楠梓杞，諸木之良也。工師者擇焉，樣稱宇棟，隨所受，無弗當者。夫人懷實入市，而棄之中衢，曰：「凡以眩人而已。」顧不大惑矣乎？《詩》曰：「藹藹王多吉士，惟君子使，媚于天子。」又曰：「藹藹王多吉人，惟君子命，媚于庶人。」言吉人之用而宜也。諸士勗哉！

刑部貴州清吏司主事屠應埈謹序。
translation_en:
…that is all. Now pian, nan, zi, and qi are among the finest timbers. The master craftsman selects them, matching their forms to the building’s beams [?]; whatever use each is assigned, none is unsuitable. If a man carries valuable goods into the marketplace but abandons them in the thoroughfare, saying, “All this is merely to dazzle people,” is he not profoundly deluded? The Book of Odes says: “In their multitude, the king’s many worthy officers are employed by the noble man and win the favor of the Son of Heaven.” It also says: “In their multitude, the king’s many worthy men receive their appointments from the noble man and win the favor of the common people.” These words speak of employing worthy men appropriately. You scholars, strive diligently!

Preface respectfully composed by Tu Yingjun, Secretary in the Guizhou Bureau of the Ministry of Justice.
